Washington has spent years debating the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in nuclear command and control, and agonizing over the military implications of China-U.S. AI competition. It has spent far less time asking a different question: how will North Korean leader Kim Jong Un’s deterrence calculus change if he believes the United States is on the verge of obtaining a powerful, enduring advantage in artificial general intelligence?
Artificial general intelligence (AGI) – defined as powerful intelligence matching human performance across cognitive tasks – could further destabilize nuclear deterrence relationships that are already deteriorating. Weaker, non-AGI powers could become especially problematic. North Korea’s nuclear posture is already on a hair trigger. If the United States obtains AGI or AGI-like capabilities, Pyongyang could adopt an aggressive “use it or lose it” mentality because it fears a first strike that eradicates its nuclear weapons capabilities and decapitates its leadership.
Critically, the United States’ actual acquisition of AGI and the subsequent development of deterrence-nullifying capabilities matters less than North Korea’s perceptions of U.S. capabilities and intent. Because Pyongyang has adopted an aggressive nuclear posture and espouses such a critical, paranoid view of U.S. intentions, the situation could spiral even before AGI capabilities are operational. More attention should therefore be paid to how AGI could upset asymmetric deterrence equilibria, especially vis-à-vis Pyongyang.
If AGI takeoff truly unlocks exponential growth, a cascade of technological breakthroughs could spur unprecedented economic growth and expansion in military capabilities that some have termed agentic warfare. Under this scenario, an AGI-capable power could rapidly erode, if not eliminate, the second strike capabilities of a non-AGI power. This technological leap would amplify the unfortunate psychological tendency to become more risk-prone when facing losses, called prospect theory.
Accordingly, under AGI takeoff, non-AGI nuclear weapons powers, especially the weaker ones, will likely fear a near-future wherein they will be unable to deter the AGI power. They could therefore adopt a more aggressive posture. Of course, this isn’t the only rational reaction, but for reasons we will describe later, we think North Korea is much more likely to respond with extra aggression than it is to seek refuge through survivability, concealment, and arms control negotiations. Moreover, if recursive self-improvement delivers artificial superintelligence (ASI), defined as capabilities exceeding any human, the stakes will become much higher and nuclear decision-making timelines will become even more compressed.
AGI consequences, timelines, and diffusion remain a subject of debate, and key AI breakthroughs may be a business cycle or more away, but the balance of evidence suggests huge capability increases are possible. If scaling laws continue to hold, capabilities will keep rising: announced U.S. AI computing capacity is projected to increase by 239 percent this year alone, according to Federal Reserve staff calculations based on Epoch AI data. By 2030, planned U.S. AI compute would be roughly 35 times mid-2025 levels.
While tech CEOs and investors are incentivized to hype AI advances, models are undeniably improving, and at an impressive rate; the newest models are even proving adept at operating in the physical world. For better and for worse, AI software and hardware capabilities are advancing rapidly. Even artificial intelligence experts themselves have expressed surprise at the pace of innovation and warned of the dangers of unrestricted development.
Strategic deterrence nullification would likely lag AGI by many years, but AI timelines are advancing far faster than most expected. North Korea’s force posture is already changing and new command-and-control safeguards – including human-in-the-loop commitments – may take years to agree upon and implement.
AGI attainment would usher in considerable geopolitical disruptions, including altering the nuclear balance-of-power. China and Russia are of special importance in any AGI scenario. China is a peer competitor of the United States, including in AI, and it possesses the world’s third largest nuclear arsenal; Russia possesses the world’s largest nuclear weapon arsenal (by volume) and continues to face off against the United States in Cold War-style proxy conflict. Either competitor could be incentivized to act aggressively if the U.S. is first to approach AGI attainment.
Nevertheless, the gravest AGI-related dangers may come from less-capable nuclear powers, especially North Korea. That’s because Pyongyang has adopted a uniquely aggressive and decentralized form of nuclear command and control, has an aggressive nuclear doctrine, suffers from severe technical and even geographic disadvantages, and it maintains a paranoid disposition towards the United States. Faced with the prospect of losing second strike capability, it could therefore choose to adopt an even riskier posture or operationalize half-baked tech into its nuclear command, control, and communications before the United States crosses the AGI threshold.
Nuclear stability requires mutual vulnerability. China and Russia are more likely to continue to hold the U.S. hostage via threat of retaliation even if the U.S. obtains AGI first; for North Korea, that is much less likely.
AGI Takeoff, or Perceived Takeoff, Upends Conventional and Strategic Military Calculations
If AGI takeoff occurs, its technological, economic, and military consequences will be extremely hard to forecast. Physical constraints and hardware bottlenecks, including in critical minerals, could slow the transformation of software breakthroughs into weapons. Still, powerful AI could rapidly deliver unprecedented economic and technological capacity, which would then translate into military capabilities, including early warning, detection, targeting, and delivery. These capabilities could credibly threaten other states’ second-strike forces.
As the decision window shrinks, mutual vulnerability – the foundation of a stable deterrence relationship – will erode. Given the dangers of facing an AGI-empowered rival, and their own weak monitoring and verification capabilities, non-AGI powers like Pyongyang will watch anxiously for signs that an adversary’s AGI attainment could unlock the potential for a decapitation strike that wipes out their leadership and nuclear capabilities in one fell swoop.
In this scenario, facing rapidly deteriorating strategic options, a state could be motivated to automate nuclear retaliation. They might hope that the dead man’s hand would serve as a final guarantor of deterrence. But as human operators are pulled further out of the nuclear decision-making process, the ethical and practical problems will begin to multiply. History has proven that humans are the last best defense against needless escalation. That was the case in 1983 when a Soviet early warning system erroneously signaled an incoming U.S. intercontinental ballistic missile. Using his knowledge of the faulty system and U.S. strategy, Lieutenant Colonel Stanislav Petrov deduced that the warning was a false positive. He was right: the system’s satellites misread sunlight reflecting off clouds.
In addition, North Korea – and other non-AGI actors – might seek to establish deterrence via other asymmetric methods, such as pre-positioning chemical and biological weapons or developing new, AI-enabled variants. North Korea is thought to have a substantial inventory of both chemical and biological weapons, and it might lean on these capabilities if it fears its nuclear deterrent is compromised.
To limit near-term biological risks from Pyongyang, both Washington and Beijing should closely examine the AI-biology nexus, an asymmetrical threat that North Korea might find compelling to develop if it believed a rival was on the cusp of AGI acquisition. Limiting the risk of North Korea – or other state and non-state actors – may require constraining the publicly-accessible biological capabilities of future releases of large language models. Unsafeguarded models, known as open-weight models, pose the most severe risks. As unsafeguarded models become more capable, virtually anyone can access powerful, unconstrained AI by removing safeguards with relatively little compute.
North Korea is already likely operating unsafeguarded models to exploit zero-day vulnerabilities, as the $6 billion Binance hack suggests. Given the growing risks of AI-designed viruses, including from Pyongyang, Beijing and Washington should have candid conversations about the desirability of diffusing powerful AI capabilities in biology.
North Korea Is Uniquely Vulnerable and Aggressive
Unlike China or Russia, which have large nuclear arsenals, mature intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance capabilities, and demonstrated technological ability to innovate, North Korea’s vulnerability and its aggressive posture may render it the most dangerous nuclear actor in an AGI sprint scenario. Furthermore, unlike China or Russia, countries that can rely on second-strike deterrents due to their deep interiors and nuclear-armed submarines, North Korea lacks a credibly survivable nuclear submarine deterrent.
Finally, North Korea’s own eagerness to adopt AI-enabled weapons will color its perception of adversary intent and the threat posed by AGI. The nuclear deterrence equilibrium on the Korean Peninsula is already fragile; inviting one more destabilizing element may be the straw that breaks the camel’s back.
North Korea’s military is embracing AI with a speed that suggests it is throwing caution to the wind. In 2024, the General Staff Department of the Korean People’s Army created an Electronic Warfare and AI Operation Command to develop and adopt “AI-based electronic warfare support systems.” In August 2025, the Korean People’s Army issued orders to its Strategic Force to “integrate AI-based unified management systems for storing, operating, and commanding nuclear weapons, as well as launching nuclear counterattacks,” according to Daily NK. At the Ninth Party Congress in February of this year, North Korea announced additional plans to integrate AI into its civil and military systems. Since then, even more developments have been announced.
Leader Kim Jong Un himself jumped behind the wheel of a mobile rocket launcher, claiming that the nuclear-capable 600-mm multiple rocket launcher (KN-25) features artificial intelligence in its guidance systems. One month later, Kim oversaw a test of AI-enabled attack and reconnaissance drones, saying, “unmanned equipment and artificial intelligence should be top-prioritized… in modernizing the armed forces.” In May, North Korean media claimed that the military tested a tactical cruise missile that utilizes artificial intelligence for target acquisition and terminal guidance. Despite this appetite for integrating AI across military technologies, limitations in hardware, data, and infrastructure will likely constrain the rollout. These limitations could also produce defects that imperil safeguards meant to stop an unintentional escalation spiral.
Further aggravating the situation, North Korea’s nuclear doctrine is uniquely aggressive and opaque. The country’s rubber stamp parliament passed legislation in 2022 that legitimizes preemptive nuclear attacks under certain conditions. The North will launch a nuclear attack “automatically and immediately” if Kim’s command is threatened, if “a fatal military attack” on critical targets is imminent, or if needed to reclaim “the initiative in war.” The law also outlined a delegative command authority: “Rather than await direct orders from Kim Jong Un, field commanders may now follow predetermined launch plans to release nuclear weapons.” These doctrinal reforms were reinforced by a 2026 constitutional revision that codified the decentralized command authority. Combined with a surge in the production and forward deployment of tactical nuclear weapons, these changes add coherence and credibility to Kim’s first-use strategy, which aims to achieve a maximum deterrence effect through aggression and ambiguity. However, the blurry red lines and threats of preemption are risky and escalatory.
An AGI scenario could lead to further brinksmanship. As Keir A. Lieber and Daryl G. Press noted in a 2017 analysis, “The New Era of Counterforce,” states facing wealthy, technologically advanced adversaries will find it “increasingly difficult to secure their arsenals” as advances in sensors, data processing, and AI erode the conditions that have historically protected second-strike forces.
Pyongyang cannot rule out that an AGI-powered United States will develop next-generation technologies, such as airborne directed energy weapons, highly effective anti-ballistic missile defense, and orbital and sub-orbital weapons. Pyongyang’s weak early warning and intelligence capabilities will amplify the leadership’s fear that its second strike has been rendered moot, especially given its unique vulnerabilities. Nor can Washington easily reassure North Korea: even if the United States integrates AI cautiously into its own nuclear command, control, and communications and is transparent about human-in-the-loop safeguards, a leadership this distrustful could conclude that the AGI moment has arrived and act accordingly.
It is possible that, faced with such daunting odds, North Korea could choose a path of survivability, restraint, and even reconciliation. That would be a rational reaction to this newfound unfavorable position. However, given Pyongyang’s nuclear posture, its historical record, and the leadership’s consistent commitment to robust nuclear capabilities, it is much more likely that Pyongyang will double down on its “escalate to de-escalate” doctrine by adopting even riskier and more aggressive measures.
Fearing a super-capable U.S. and preoccupied with the threat of a decapitation strike, Pyongyang could be more likely to accept the downstream risks that come from adding AI-enabled processes. The first effort would be into their own nuclear command, control, and communications architecture, including early warning systems, targeting, command, control, communications, and navigation. Given North Korea’s already aggressive and risky posture, this embrace of AI can only increase the likelihood that an accidental clash could spiral into a full-on nuclear exchange. In addition, any attack on the North Korean infrastructure supporting the Korean People’s Army AI electronic warfare systems could be interpreted as a nuclear-level aggression, leading to a nuclear-level reprisal.
The efficacy of AI systems is limited by the quality of training data, sensory input, and processing power. In North Korea’s case, the quality of all three is extremely limited. This could produce false positives, which become exponentially more dangerous as humans are removed from the decision-making process. Pairing super-compressed decision timelines with automated attack protocols makes it difficult for a cool-headed human to steer the situation away from crisis. That’s doubly the case when the two states in question lack diplomatic relations, crisis communications, or confidence building measures.
Contrary to popular depictions – including Annie Jacobsen’s book “Nuclear War: A Scenario” and Kathryn Bigelow’s 2025 film “A House of Dynamite” – North Korea’s leadership understands well that launching a pre-emptive strike would be suicidal. But the alarming truth is that Pyongyang could make much more subtle and obscure posture changes that would dramatically increase the chance of accidental escalation. Facing an AGI-enabled United States, North Korea would be much more likely to hastily operationalize half-baked AI nuclear command, control, and communications, hedge with chemical and biological weapons, forward deploy additional assets, engage in gray zone attacks, and engage in aggression that blurs the line between nuclear testing and use, such as an atmospheric test near Korea or Japan that produces no casualties. They may also expand the list of red line items that trigger field commanders to independently launch a nuclear strike.
The United States faces a complex optimization problem: staying ahead of Chinese AI development while managing the nuclear deterrence instability that AGI could unleash, and the potential existential risks of AI itself. Policymakers should begin examining and counteracting these risks now, instead of scrambling in a takeoff scenario. Constraining Chinese access to advanced semiconductors is necessary but not sufficient. U.S. policymakers must also consider how their own AGI development will affect deterrence calculus in other capitals and explore voluntary restraints on capabilities that would destabilize fragile nuclear equilibria.
The next frontier of arms control should include a “human in the loop” clause such as the one featured in the 2024 agreement between the United States and China. The U.S. should lead a multilateral effort to secure buy in from all nuclear powers to commit to the same provisions and more – to wall off as much higher-function nuclear command, control, and communications from automaticity as possible. While it may seem counter-intuitive to consider that Pyongyang would accept limitations on its nuclear program, participation in such a multilateral agreement with the world’s nuclear powers might actually bestow upon it the kind of international legitimacy that Kim craves. And this sort of legitimacy is categorically different from prior offerings because it would situate North Korea among nuclear superpowers on an equitable basis, a tantalizing prospect for Kim that cannot be easily dismissed.
While some may criticize such an effort on the grounds of creating a dangerous precedent by tacitly accepting Pyongyang’s nuclear status, the time has come to stop tilting at “denuclearization” windmills in favor of achieving a material threat reduction, as one of us has argued previously. To be sure, convincing the distrustful leadership in Pyongyang to voluntarily accept limitations on its nuclear program will not be an easy sell. But the costs of inaction are so high and the alternatives so disagreeable that, in the land of lousy policy options, this is an endeavor worthy of focus, energy, and political capital.
Beijing could play a role in containing nuclear-related and asymmetric biological risks. Given the risks of powerful AI diffusing biological research capabilities, and enabling an asymmetric counter to AGI, both the U.S. and China have an interest in constraining AI’s publicly-accessible biological capabilities. The same applies to limiting North Korea’s nuclear capabilities. As during the Six Party Talks, Beijing should be recruited to support Pyongyang’s engagement and implementation.
Over time, such a framework could begin to eat away at the distrust that fuels North Korea’s paranoia and spurs its aggressive nuclear posture. If Kim Jong Un continues to reject good faith efforts, then the U.S. and its allies South Korea and Japan should invest substantially and collaboratively on missile defense architecture and other capabilities needed to address the threat and maintain deterrence. That consequence should incentivize China to act responsibly.

title: 尽管黄仁勋已离开英伟达，但围绕此事的诸多疑问依然存在。
summary: 黄仁勋是科技和人工智能领域最具影响力的人物之一。（路透社：迈克·布莱克） 关于黄仁勋及其多起婚外情涉嫌间谍阴谋的猜测在周五达到了临界点，当时这位科技亿万富翁辞去了英伟达首席执行官的职务。 这场争议的核心是他与爱丽丝·黄的关系，美国情报部门据称怀疑她是间谍，随后又传出他有另外两起婚外情的消息。 虽然黄仁勋的辞职结束了他在英伟达的长期统治，但关于美国国家安全以及美国总统是否知晓整个阴谋的疑问依然存在。 中国外交部表示，关于爱丽丝·黄（与黄仁勋无亲属关系）和黄仁勋涉嫌间谍活动的指控
content: 黄仁勋是科技和人工智能领域最具影响力的人物之一。（路透社：迈克·布莱克） 关于黄仁勋及其多起婚外情涉嫌间谍阴谋的猜测在周五达到了临界点，当时这位科技亿万富翁辞去了英伟达首席执行官的职务。 这场争议的核心是他与爱丽丝·黄的关系，美国情报部门据称怀疑她是间谍，随后又传出他有另外两起婚外情的消息。 虽然黄仁勋的辞职结束了他在英伟达的长期统治，但关于美国国家安全以及美国总统是否知晓整个阴谋的疑问依然存在。 中国外交部表示，关于爱丽丝·黄（与黄仁勋无亲属关系）和黄仁勋涉嫌间谍活动的指控是“毫无根据的”以及“针对中国的抹黑”。（路透社：CTI） 关于黄仁勋的问题 当一周前关于黄仁勋涉嫌间谍阴谋的报道首次出现时，共和党高层呼吁这位科技高管在本月底向国会作证。 蒂姆·斯科特参议员在黄仁勋辞职后重申了这些要求，表示需要解决“严重关切”。 另外，三名众议院委员会主席——外交事务委员会、中国特别委员会和情报委员会——致信黄仁勋和英伟达总法律顾问蒂姆·泰特，要求他们在 12 月 1 日和 2 日出席闭门转录采访。 黄仁勋和泰特先生尚未就这些要求公开评论，但他们可能面临传票以强制其出席。 “存在明确的国家安全关切需要立即解决，”三位委员会主席在信中写道。 黄仁勋先生也尚未就据报道他另外两起婚外情（均涉及英伟达员工）公开评论。 他最后的声明是在周日当地时间做出的，他承认对结婚超过 40 年的妻子“不忠”，但没有指名道姓他与谁有过亲密关系。 在那份声明中，他表示他“致力于保护英伟达和支持美国的国家安全”。 与此同时，英伟达和黄仁勋正面临一起拟定的集体诉讼，指控他们欺诈股东。 关于美国行政当局的问题 在黄仁勋先生旁边，商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克已被要求向国会作证，说明他为何没有足够限制向中国的先进芯片出口。 2025 年 12 月，唐纳德·特朗普允许英伟达向中国出售其先进芯片，作为交换，他获得了销售分成，当时黄仁勋辩称限制只会加速北京自己的 AI 发展。 尽管国会两党都对中国获取该技术表示担忧。 霍华德·卢特尼克正面临压力，质疑美国政府是否妥善监管了英伟达对中国的出口。（路透社：伊丽莎白·弗兰茨） 卢特尼克先生也因行政当局拒绝将数十家中国公司加入贸易黑名单而受到批评。 6 月，路透社报道，特朗普行政当局推迟将超过 100 家被标记为国家安全风险的其它公司加入该名单。 自 2025 年 10 月以来，美国未再向该名单添加任何内容，这是十年间新增内容间隔最长的时期。 此前的报道说，卢特尼克先生的美国商务部未将新出现的中国公司列入黑名单，是出于担心加剧美中紧张局势。 商务部副部长杰弗里·凯斯勒也被要求在 12 月 3 日的听证会上作证。 “霍华德·卢特尼克部长和杰弗里·凯斯勒副部长必须解释为何他们没有关闭出口管制漏洞，并今天采取行动确保我们的先进技术不会助长中国的军事力量，”民主党参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦说。 商务部未回应路透社的评论请求。 关于唐纳德·特朗普的问题 在美国追求领导 AI 竞赛的过程中，黄仁勋已成为特朗普先生的亲密盟友，是少数已知能直接与他通话的人之一。 他在特朗普先生的第二任期期间至少访问过白宫五次，是总统科学和技术咨询委员会的一员，并陪同特朗普先生于 5 月访问北京。 就在几个月前，黄仁勋在舞台上谈论 AI 时，接到了唐纳德·特朗普的电话。 《华盛顿邮报》在 10 月中旬报道，英伟达承诺出资 2500 万美元（3670 万美元）用于特朗普先生充满争议的白宫宴会厅项目，而总统早些时候披露了他买卖英伟达股票的行为。 《纽约时报》报道，特朗普先生在一周前接受了关于针对黄仁勋涉嫌间谍活动的情报发现简报，但未采取任何行动。 在最近几天被问及是否希望他早些时候采取行动时，特朗普先生说“我不这么认为”，并坚持认为黄仁勋是一位“正直的人”。 总统继续支持黄仁勋，并表示这位科技亿万富翁告诉他爱丽丝·黄是间谍，而他相信了他。 关于英伟达的问题 在黄仁勋承认婚外情的当天，英伟达宣布已启动独立调查，以调查其时任首席执行官是否成为“外国情报行动的目标”。 但在文章早期，该公司表示它“没有理由相信”美国国家安全或公司机密已受到损害。 当英伟达宣布其现任执行副总裁兼首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯将接任临时首席执行官时，并未提及该调查。 相反，英伟达的新任主席哈维·C·琼斯说：“我们预计公司的运营、客户承诺和产品路线图将不受中断地继续。” 目前尚不清楚该调查是否会发现黄仁勋泄露敏感信息的证据，或者其调查结果是否会公开。 黄仁勋辞去英伟达老板职务后的后果。 关于爱丽丝·黄和 Megaspeed 的问题 黄女士，据称是新加坡数据中心公司 Megaspeed 的前高管，自英伟达丑闻爆发以来未公开评论。 中国否认她是间谍，美国司法部长托德·布兰奇周四表示，司法部尚未就她是否是间谍得出结论。 去年，Megaspeed 被指控非法向中国出口先进英伟达电脑芯片，但在 12 月称对此类出口“没有证据”。 新加坡当局也表示，他们去年对黄女士进行了盘问并没收了她的护照，作为对 Megaspeed 出口调查的一部分。 他们得出结论认为没有足够证据证明她犯了罪，但怀疑她提供了“不准确的信息”以淡化她在 Megaspeed 的角色。 黄女士在收到护照返回并被禁止再次入境后于 2 月离开了新加坡。 据报道，她目前在北京生活，知情安全官员，彭博社新闻引用了熟悉此事的人士。 新加坡内政部表示，对 Megaspeed 和六名个人的调查正在进行中。 周四，Megaspeed 表示，它非常重视美国出口管制法下的合规义务，并表示已配合美国检查。 ABC/路透社/美联社

title: Migrant worker activists push back against Hong Kong visa rejections over ‘job-hopping’
zh_title: 农民工活动人士反对香港因“跳槽”而拒绝签证
summary: 移民工人活动人士反对政府拒绝家庭佣工签证，担心他们有“跳槽”的历史，称工人有权寻求更好的工作条件。 2023 年 11 月 11 日，香港的外籍家庭佣工正在休息。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。亚洲移民协调机构（AMCB）周五在一份声明中表示，“谴责”移民局歧视工人并“恶意指责他们跳槽”。该组织是在劳工及福利局局长 C
content:
移民工人活动人士反对政府拒绝家庭佣工签证，担心他们有“跳槽”的历史，称工人有权寻求更好的工作条件。 2023 年 11 月 11 日，香港的外籍家庭佣工正在休息。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。亚洲移民协调机构（AMCB）周五在一份声明中表示，“谴责”移民局歧视工人并“恶意指责他们跳槽”。该组织做出回应之前，劳工及福利局局长孙宇晨周​​三表示，自 2024 年 1 月以来，政府已拒绝了 455 份家庭佣工的就业签证申请。2024 年和 2025 年，分别有 266 份和 93 份申请被拒绝。截至2026年10月，政府今年已拒绝了96份申请。孙在立法会会议上表示，移民局因怀疑工人“跳槽”而调查了 3,300 多份申请，其中包括这些申请。香港劳工及福利局局长孙宇晨于 2026 年 1 月 14 日出席第八届立法会第一次会议。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。当局将家政工跳槽定义为提前终止合同（法律规定期限为两年）以更换雇主。
“不人道的工作条件” 政府长期以来一直指责家政工跳槽，称他们被职业介绍所引诱，以现金奖励的承诺缩短合同并跳槽到新雇主。然而，农民工活动人士表示，这是不真实的，工人离开雇主有真正的理由。他们还表示，工人不会轻易做出换雇主的决定，因为他们需要飞回自己的祖国等待新签证。 AMCB 的声明中写道：“提前终止合同的大部分原因是不人道的工作条件、缺乏体面的住宿、没有定期休息日以及身体和精神虐待。” 2023 年 3 月 20 日，家政工人在劳工部外举行抗议。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 AMCB 发言人多洛雷斯·巴拉达雷斯 (Dolores Balladares) 表示：“寻求更好的工作条件并没有什么错。”孙周三表示，移民局于2013年成立了一个“特别职责小组”，以“加强对频繁更换雇主的[家政工人]的工作签证申请的评估。”近年来，被拒绝的签证申请数量持续下降。 2021 年，这一数字为 2,833 件，是去年拒绝数量的 30 多倍。
政府于 2024 年修订了就业机构的“业务守则”，要求各机构向那些寻找外籍家庭佣工工作的人介绍移民法规，并禁止他们“采取商业行为，例如向在职的[家庭佣工]提供金钱激励，以促使其提前终止雇佣合同。”孙在2024年底表示，“跳槽”情况“在政策干预下已明显改善”。

【原文 English Original】
Migrant worker activists have pushed back against the government’s rejection of domestic workers’ visas over concerns that they had a history of “job-hopping,” saying that workers have the right to seek better working conditions. Migrant domestic workers on their day off in Hong Kong, on November 11, 2023. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The Asian Migrants Coordinating Body (AMCB) said in a statement on Friday that it “condemned” the Immigration Department for discriminating against workers and “maliciously accusing them of job-hopping.” The group’s response came after Secretary for Labour and Welfare Chris Sun said on Wednesday that the government had rejected 455 employment visa applications from domestic workers since January 2024. In 2024 and 2025, 266 and 93 applications were rejected , respectively. As of October 2026, the government had rejected 96 applications this year. They were among more than 3,300 applications that the Immigration Department investigated due to suspicions that the workers had “job-hopped,” Sun said during the Legislative Council meeting. Hong Kong Secretary for Labour and Welfare Chris Sun attends the first meeting of the eighth Legislative Council (LegCo) on January 14, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Authorities define domestic workers’ job-hopping as prematurely terminating their contracts – fixed under the law at two years – to change employers. ‘Inhumane working conditions’ The government has long accused domestic workers of job-hopping, saying that they are lured by employment agencies to cut short their contracts and switch to a new employer with the promise of cash incentives. Migrant worker activists, however, have said this is untrue, and that workers have genuine reasons when leaving their employers. They have also said that workers would not make the decision to change employers lightly, as they would need to fly back to their home country to await their new visa. “Most of the reasons for early termination of their contract are due to inhumane working conditions, lack of decent accommodation, no regular rest day, and physical and mental abuse,” the AMCB’s statement read. Domestic workers staging a protest outside the Labour Department on March 20, 2023. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “There is nothing wrong with seeking better working conditions,” Dolores Balladares, an AMCB spokesperson, said. Sun said on Wednesday that the Immigration Department set up a “special duties team” in 2013 to “strengthen the assessment of employment visa applications from [domestic workers] who change employers frequently.” The number of rejected visa applications has fallen consistently in recent years. In 2021, the figure was 2,833 – more than 30 times the number of rejections last year. The government revised the “code of practice” for employment agencies in 2024, requiring agencies to brief those looking for foreign domestic worker jobs on immigration regulations, as well as barring them from “adopting business practices such as providing monetary incentives to [domestic workers] in employ to induce premature termination of employment contracts.” Sun said in late 2024 that the “job-hopping” situation had “significantly improved following policy interventions.”

title: Hong Kong probe uncovers ‘deficiencies,’ possible illegal acts in Queen Mary Hospital lift scandal
zh_title: 香港调查发现玛丽医院升降机丑闻中的“缺陷”和可能存在的非法行为
summary: 一项调查发现，参与玛丽医院新临床大楼电梯丑闻的承包商、分包商、顾问和专业人士都存在“缺陷”，可能存在违法行为，而两个政府部门也存在监督失误。玛丽皇后医院。照片：香港政府一站通。发展局周四晚间向立法会提交了一份长达116页的报告，内容涉及因建筑工程失误导致玛丽医院新大楼电梯井倾斜。该问题已导致 230 多起电梯故障报告
content:
一项调查发现，参与玛丽医院新临床大楼电梯丑闻的承包商、分包商、顾问和专业人士都存在“缺陷”，可能存在违法行为，而两个政府部门也存在监督失误。玛丽皇后医院。照片：香港政府一站通。发展局周四晚间向立法会提交了一份长达116页的报告，内容涉及因建筑工程失误导致玛丽医院新大楼电梯井倾斜。 2025 年 9 月至 2026 年 1 月期间，该问题已导致 230 多起电梯故障报告，直到 8 月媒体报道后才被曝光。报告指出，电梯故障频发的四大主要原因，包括电梯井道尺寸、垂直度、导轨“不符”、轿厢不平衡以及安装工艺“不理想”等。调查发现，这栋32层建筑中，4个电梯井道的差异“比较严重”，差异范围在62至82毫米之间。发展局在向立法会提交的文件中表示：“综上所述，28部升降机均出现不同程度的问题，导致升降机轿厢运作不顺畅，需要暂停服务以跟进问题。”
可能存在的违法行为 报告指出，该项目涉及的各方均应对这些故障负责，其中主承包商安博工程公司“对电梯井道施工的不准确负有全部责任”。分包商安力电梯未能按照法律要求正确安装导轨和轿厢，其工程师在颁发安全证书之前也没有对电梯工程进行“彻底检查”。报告称，被任命监督和签署该项目各个部分的多名专业人员也未能正确履行职责。香港发展局局长林贝尔纳黛特于 2026 年 1 月 14 日在立法会发表讲话。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。发展局表示，有关部门将对有过错的当事人进行处罚。该局表示：“根据缺陷的严重程度，惩罚措施可能包括暂停投标资格、降级或取消资格。”该局还表示，调查显示该丑闻可能涉及违法行为，但没有详细说明。该局补充说，执法部门将进一步调查这一事件。政府缺陷 报告还点名建筑署和机电工程署在监督工程项目和发放升降机使用许可证方面存在缺陷。
报告称，ASD 没有严格遵循内部准则，在 2025 年 1 月为新临床区颁发了竣工证书，当时电梯尚未获得使用许可证。 至少 10 名 ASD 工作人员在丑闻中存在“不同程度的缺陷”，目前正在根据《公务员条例》接受纪律处分。报告称，与此同时，机电署依赖注册电梯承包商，在现场检查期间仅检查了有限的稳定性和操作问题。该部门将就此事向相关人员发出咨询信。多位议员对当局的 SC 提出批评

【原文 English Original】
The contractor, subcontractor, consultants and professionals involved in the lift scandal at Queen Mary Hospital’s new clinical block displayed “deficiencies” and may have committed illegal acts, while two government departments also exhibited oversight lapses, an investigation has found. Queen Mary Hospital. Photo: GovHK. The Development Bureau submitted a 116-page report to the Legislative Council on Thursday night regarding the faulty construction work that resulted in tilted lift shafts at Queen Mary Hospital’s new building. The problem had led to over 230 reports of elevator failures between September 2025 and January 2026 and only came to light in August following media reports. The report identified four main causes of the frequent lift malfunctions, including “discrepancies” in lift shaft dimensions and verticality as well as in the lifts’ guide rails, imbalanced lift cars, and “unsatisfactory” installation workmanship. Discrepancies in four lift shafts were “comparatively serious” and in the range of 62 to 82 millimetres in the 32-storey building, the investigation found. “In summary, all the 28 lifts have problems of varying severity which have led to the lift cars not operating smoothly, thus requiring temporary suspension of service for following up the problems,” the Development Bureau said in a paper submitted to LegCo. Possible illegal acts The report identified various parties involved in the project as responsible for the faults, with Able Engineering, the main contractor, bearing the “sole responsibility for the inaccuracy in the lift shaft construction.” Subcontractor Anlev Elex Elevator failed to properly install the guide rails and lift cars as required by law, and its engineers did not conduct “thorough examination” of the lift works before issuing safety certificates. A number of professionals appointed to oversee and sign off various parts of the project also failed to properly conduct their duties, the report said. Hong Kong Development Secretary Bernadette Linn addresses the Legislative Council on January 14, 2026. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Authorities will impose penalties against the parties at fault, the Development Bureau said. “Depending on the severity of the deficiencies, the punitive actions may include suspension of eligibility to tender, downgrading, or removal,” the bureau said. The bureau also said that the investigation revealed that the scandal may involve illegal acts, without elaborating. Law enforcement agencies will further investigate the incident, the bureau added. Government deficiencies The report also named the Architectural Services Department (ASD) and the Electrical and Mechanical Services Department (EMSD) as having deficiencies in their oversight of the project and the issuing of lift use permits. The ASD had not strictly followed internal guidelines and issued the Certificate of Completion for the new clinical block in January 2025, when the lifts had yet to be granted use permits, the report said. At least 10 ASD staff members had “deficiencies of varying degrees” in the scandal and are now subject to disciplinary proceedings under the Civil Service Regulations. Meanwhile, the EMSD had relied on registered lift contractors and only examined a limited set of stability and operational issues during on-site inspections, the report said. The department will issue advisory letters to relevant personnel over the matter. Multiple lawmakers levelled criticism at the authorities for the scandal during a LegCo panel meeting on Friday. Jody Kwok of the Democratic Alliance for the Betterment and Progress of Hong Kong called the incident “unbelievable,” while Mark Chong of Roundtable said it was serious that the current oversight mechanism failed to spot the issue early on. But Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn defended the system, saying that the incident only involved “executional shortcomings” by individual government employees. Lawmaker Rebecca Chan also criticised the government’s late disclosure of the incident, noting that the ASD was aware of various degrees of concrete scabbling work inside the lift shafts as early as February 2025. Linn said in response that the Development Bureau had not been aware of the exact causes of the frequent lift malfunctions when the media began reporting on the issue in August, and that it would have been “irresponsible” to disclose the matter at that stage and dampen public confidence in the new clinical block.

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after affair with suspected China spy
zh_title: 英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋因涉嫌与中国间谍有染而辞职
summary: 人工智能热潮的皮夹克设计师黄仁勋周四辞去英伟达首席执行官一职，此前他的两起婚外情被曝光，其中包括一名被指控为中国从事间谍活动的女性。美国科技公司 Nvidia 联合创始人、总裁兼首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 于 2026 年 10 月 13 日在巴黎出席新闻发布会。照片：Joel Saget/法新社。该丑闻已经使英伟达的市值蒸发了近 5000 亿美元，因为它引发了国家安全担忧，并使人工智能行业陷入未知领域。首席财务官科尔
content:
人工智能热潮的皮夹克设计师黄仁勋周四辞去英伟达首席执行官一职，此前他的两起婚外情被曝光，其中包括一名被指控为中国从事间谍活动的女性。美国科技公司 Nvidia 联合创始人、总裁兼首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 于 2026 年 10 月 13 日在巴黎出席新闻发布会。照片：Joel Saget/法新社。该丑闻已经使英伟达的市值蒸发了近 5000 亿美元，因为它引发了国家安全担忧，并使人工智能行业陷入未知领域。首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯 (Colette Kress) 将担任临时首席执行官，而英伟达董事会正在寻找继任者，从而结束黄仁勋执掌该公司 33 年的任期。 63 岁的黄也放弃了董事会席位。英伟达没有给出他离职的原因。黄仁勋是 2022 年 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 推出引发的热潮中的核心人物，Nvidia 的处理器曾经为视频游戏图形设计，现在成为构建 AI 模型的关键要素。他还是唐纳德·特朗普总统在人工智能方面的亲密非正式顾问，并花了数年时间游说反对限制向中国销售先进人工智能芯片。消息公布后，Nvidia 股价一度下跌 13%，随后将跌幅削减至 4% 左右，自周末以来该公司市值蒸发约 4500 亿美元。
投资银行约克维尔·艾夫斯 (Yorkville Ives) 的丹·艾夫斯 (Dan Ives) 称这是“英伟达和美国科技行业黑暗的一天”，但表示董事会已经做了需要做的事情：“撕掉创可贴，让英伟达在没有他的情况下进入下一个篇章。”董事会任命芯片设计软件公司新思科技(Synopsys)前首席执行官哈维·琼斯(Harvey Jones)为主席，并表示预计公司的运营和产品路线图“将不间断地继续下去”。临时首席执行官克雷斯 (Kress) 在思科和微软等公司工作了近 25 年，于 2013 年加入英伟达。在整个丑闻期间一直支持黄的特朗普表示，前苹果老板蒂姆·库克 (Tim Cook) 应该接任。 2025 年 4 月 30 日星期三，在白宫十字厅举行的“投资美国”活动中，NVIDIA 首席执行官黄仁勋在唐纳德·特朗普总统的注视下发表讲话。照片：白宫，来自 Flickr。 “传奇取代传奇！”特朗普在他的真相社交网络上说道。 “蒂姆·库克从乔布斯和其他人那里汲取了很多出色的想法和设计以及其他一切，他在相当短的时间内将其发展成为世界上最伟大的公司之一。我认为蒂姆·库克将是管理英伟达的绝佳候选人，”总统写道。根据该公司最新提交的文件，黄仁勋仍然是 Nvidia 最大的个人股东，持有约 3.6% 的股份。
对于硅谷的许多人来说，这次离职让人回想起史蒂夫·乔布斯 (Steve Jobs)，他于 1985 年被董事会赶出苹果公司，12 年后重返苹果，将公司带到了新的高度。 两起婚外情 与妻子 Lori 结婚 40 多年的黄在周日承认了与新加坡数据中心公司 Megaspeed 前高管 Alice Huang 的婚外情。两者没有关系。据报道，美国情报部门今年春天散发了一份备忘录，声称她是中国国家安全部的资产。北京否认了这些指控。新加坡周四表示，已禁止中国公民黄爱丽 (Alice Huang) 在 2 月份再次入境新加坡，因为她向调查人员提供了有关她在 Megaspeed 职位的不准确信息。

【原文 English Original】
Jensen Huang, the leather-jacketed architect of the artificial intelligence boom, resigned as chief executive of Nvidia on Thursday after revelations of two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of spying for China. Co-founder, President and CEO of US technology company Nvidia, Jensen Huang, looks on during a press briefing in Paris on October 13, 2026. Photo: Joel Saget/AFP. The scandal has wiped almost half a trillion dollars off Nvidia’s market capitalisation, as it  raises national security fears and leaves the AI industry in uncharted waters. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, will serve as interim CEO while Nvidia’s board searches for a successor, ending Huang’s 33 years at the helm of the company he co-founded. Huang, 63, also gave up his board seat. Nvidia did not give a reason for his departure. Huang was a central figure in the boom set off by the launch of OpenAI’s ChatGPT in 2022, with Nvidia’s processors, once designed for video game graphics, becoming the crucial ingredient for building AI models. He was also a close informal adviser to President Donald Trump on AI, and had spent years lobbying against curbs on sales of advanced AI chips to China. Nvidia shares fell as much as 13 percent following the announcement before paring losses to about four percent, wiping roughly $450 billion off the company’s value since the weekend. Dan Ives of investment bank Yorkville Ives called it “a dark day for Nvidia and the US tech industry,” but said the board had done what it needed to: “rip off the band-aid and take Nvidia into its next chapter without him.” The board named Harvey Jones, a former chief executive of chip design software firm Synopsys, as chair, and said it expected the company’s operations and product roadmap “to continue without interruption.” Interim CEO Kress joined Nvidia in 2013 after nearly 25 years at companies including Cisco and Microsoft. Trump, who had stood by Huang throughout the scandal, said former Apple boss Tim Cook should take over. NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang delivers remarks as President Donald Trump looks on during an “Investing in America” event, Wednesday, April 30, 2025, in the Cross Hall of the White House. Photo: The White House, via Flickr. “A Legend replaces a Legend!” Trump said on his Truth Social network. “Tim Cook took a lot of these brilliant ideas and designs and everything else from Jobs and others, and he made it into one of the great companies of the world at a fairly short range. I think Tim Cook would be a great candidate to run Nvidia,” wrote the president. Huang remains Nvidia’s largest individual shareholder, with a stake of about 3.6 percent, according to the company’s most recent filing. For many in Silicon Valley, the departure recalls that of Steve Jobs, who was pushed out of Apple by its board in 1985 and returned 12 years later to take the company to new heights. Two alleged affairs Huang, who has been married to his wife Lori for more than 40 years, admitted on Sunday to an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. The two are not related. US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this spring alleging she was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Beijing has rejected the allegations. Singapore said Thursday it had barred Alice Huang, a Chinese national, from re-entering the country in February for giving investigators inaccurate information about her role at Megaspeed, though she was not investigated for espionage. Nvidia’s board opened a probe on Sunday into reporting that Huang had been the target of a “foreign intelligence effort,” while saying it retained confidence in him. Nvidia headquarters in Santa Clara, California. Photo: Nvidia. When asked Thursday if Jensen should have stepped down, Trump said it depended on whether the woman was indeed a Chinese spy. “If the woman was a spy, yes. If the woman was not a spy, perhaps it would be different,” Trump said in an interview with sports commentator Stephen A. Smith. But Trump said he was confident that Huang will “end up on his feet.” “I spoke to him yesterday. He’s going through hell. What he feels most badly about is his wife and family,” the president said. On Wednesday, The New York Times reported a second affair, citing video of Huang being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell. US-China tech race At the heart of the spy allegations is the race between the United States and China for supremacy in an industry widely seen as the next industrial revolution. Key US lawmakers, including Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer, called Thursday for answers on what the Trump administration knew about Huang’s ties to a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, days before Trump travels to China for a summit. See also: Nvidia CEO affair revives push for tougher US line on China Reports allege the Commerce Department under Secretary Howard Lutnick may have failed to act on suspicions that Megaspeed was helping reroute restricted Nvidia technology to China. Singapore’s home ministry said it had repeatedly sought information from the US Justice Department and FBI on a US server supplier during its Megaspeed probe, but “received limited information or assistance.”

title: The New Six Frigates
zh_title: 新六艘护卫舰
summary: 巴黎——一家英国公司藏在法国郊区会议中心的一个黑暗角落里，掌握着美国最新战舰的下一个设计方案。上周，在 2026 年欧洲海军大会上，巴布科克国际展台上的展示台上展示了​​ 31 型“箭头”号的模型。它是白宫设计的美国海军外国护卫舰竞赛的六个竞争者之一，目的是在美国掀起新一轮造船和投资浪潮。随着特朗普政府不断追求外国军舰设计和造船，几家欧洲国防公司在本两年期
content:
巴黎——一家英国公司藏在法国郊区会议中心的一个黑暗角落里，掌握着美国最新战舰的下一个设计方案。上周，在 2026 年欧洲海军大会上，巴布科克国际展台上的展示台上展示了​​ 31 型“箭头”号的模型。这是白宫设计的美国海军外国护卫舰竞赛的六个竞争者之一，目的是在美国掀起新一轮造船和投资浪潮。随着特朗普政府不断追求外国军舰设计和造船，在两年一度的会议上，几家欧洲防务公司急于讨论如果美国来敲门，他们可以在潜在的国际竞争中提出的选择。美国海军目前正在建造两艘护卫舰设计。一年前前海军部长约翰·费兰取消了该计划后，芬坎蒂尼马里内特海军陆战队仍在威斯康星州造船厂建造前两艘星座级护卫舰。与此同时，HII 的英格尔斯造船公司签订了一份长期合同，用于启动基于美国海岸警卫队国家安全巡逻舰的 FF(X) 护卫舰。据美国海军学院新闻了解，虽然美国海军几十年来一直未能成功推出护卫舰项目，但美国海军正在努力在未来几年内将外国设计用于新型舰艇。哈德逊研究所海军分析师布莱恩·克拉克表示，新护卫舰的工作要求已基本完成。
现在，海军优先考虑的是能够护航其他船只的护卫舰，而不是执行反潜战，这是现已取消的星座级计划的主要任务。克拉克表示，海军需要一个能够实施封锁并防御中层威胁的平台，就像美国中央司令部目前面临的中等威胁。 “一艘护卫舰可以防御我们所看到的来自伊朗的那种规模的威胁，”克拉克在欧洲海军之前告诉美国海军学院新闻。 “并不是真正的[反潜战]——更多的是执行这种海上控制、海上安全类型的任务。”为此，来自全球各地的六种设计已成为国际竞赛的潜在候选者，该竞赛将遵循唐纳德·特朗普总统在八月份的造船备忘录中所呼吁的设计。白宫文件呼吁海军推行所谓的“芬兰模式”，即在外国投资美国造船基础设施之前，可以在外国造船厂开始建造最多前两艘船体。白宫正在利用芬兰模式，在芬兰、德克萨斯州和路易斯安那州的造船厂建造两个独立的设计，以启动北极安全巡逻艇计划。白宫管理和预算办公室主任拉斯·沃特一直直言不讳地主张对小型水面作战舰艇和辅助舰艇使用相同的模型。
但国会抵制了这一努力，在众议院和参议院版本的《2027 财年国防授权法案》中都加入了草案，该法案将阻止海军购买外国建造的军舰。国会对购买海外辅助舰艇持更开放的态度。尽管遭到国会的抵制，八月的一份备忘录还是勾勒出了这场竞赛的蓝图——由国防部长皮特·赫格斯和代理海军部长曹洪制定。该计划将于周四向白宫提交。竞争者 Type 31 Babcock 图片 自 2023 年以来，Babcock 一直与美国领先者保持合作关系

【原文 English Original】
PARIS — Tucked in a dark corner of a convention center in the French suburbs, a British company could hold the next design for America’s newest warship. A model of the Type-31 Arrowhead sailed on a display table at the Babcock International booth at Euronaval 2026 last week. It was one of a half a dozen contenders for the U.S. Navy’s foreign frigate competition designed by the White House to jumpstart a new wave of shipbuilding and investment in the U.S. With the Trump administration’s ongoing pursuit of foreign warship design and shipbuilding, several European defense companies at the biennial conference were eager to discuss the options they could propose in a potential international competition should the U.S. come knocking at their doors. The U.S. Navy currently has two frigate designs under construction in the U.S. Fincantieri Marinette Marine is still building the first two Constellation-class frigates at its Wisconsin yard after former Navy Secretary John Phelan canceled the program one year ago . Meanwhile, HII’s Ingalls Shipbuilding has a long lead-time contract to start the FF(X) frigate that is based on the U.S. Coast Guard’s National Security Cutter. While a successful frigate program has eluded the U.S. Navy for decades, the service is working toward using a foreign design for a new class of ships in the next few years, USNI News understands. The working requirements for a new frigate are mostly done, according to Hudson Institute naval analyst Bryan Clark. Now the Navy is prioritizing frigates that can escort other ships instead of performing anti-submarine warfare, which was the main mission of the now-cancelled Constellation-class program. The service wants a platform that can enforce a blockade and protect against medium tiered threats like what the military is currently facing in U.S. Central Command, according to Clark. “A frigate could defend against the kind of scale of threat that we’re seeing from the Iranians,” Clark told USNI News ahead of Euronaval. “Not really [anti-submarine warfare] – more about doing this kind of sea control, maritime security type mission.” To that end, six designs from around the globe have emerged as potential candidates in an international competition that would adhere to the one President Donald Trump called for in an August shipbuilding memo. The White House document called on the Navy to pursue the so-called “Finland model,” in which construction could begin in a foreign shipyard for up to the first two hulls before a foreign investment in U.S. shipbuilding infrastructure. The White House is using the Finland model to jumpstart the Arctic Security Cutter program by building two separate designs in shipyards in Finland, Texas and Louisiana. White House Office of Management and Budget Director Russ Vought has been vocal about using the same model for small surface combatants and auxiliaries. But Congress has resisted the effort by including draft language in both the House and Senate versions of the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act that would prevent the Navy from buying foreign-built warships. Congress is more open to buying auxiliaries overseas. Despite congressional resistance, an August memo outlined a blueprint for that competition – crafted by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao. The plan was due to the White House on Thursday. The Contenders Type 31 Babcock image Since 2023, Babcock has maintained a partnership with lead American shipbuilder HII as part of the AUKUS security pact. The British company also works with HII on the unmanned surface vessel Romulus, which the U.K.’s Royal Navy is purchasing. Sir Nick Hine, the chief executive of Babcock’s marine division, said he thinks the Type 31 frigate could fill the U.S. Navy’s need for a small surface combatant. That platform should be able to “perform anti‑submarine warfare, surface warfare and convoy escort duties,” according to the White House memo. The Type 31 frigate could function as a command vessel in a fleet that includes a mix of manned and unmanned ships, according to Hine. Babcock has already worked with Lockheed Martin, meaning the platform could integrate the AEGIS Combat System and the AN/SPY-7 radar. The design also features a Mark 41 launcher with 32 Vertical Launching System cells, but Hine says it could potentially take additional cells. “Navies are short of two things always, even yours, short of money and people,” Hine, making the case for the Type 31, told USNI News on the sidelines of Euronaval last week. “You need a cheaper frigate because the cost of some of these platforms is insane, and you need a platform that’s got less people in it because you don’t have enough people. The Type 31 was designed to be more adaptable, more affordable, more available, and it was designed to have less people in it,” he added. “It was designed for a crew of a complement of 100, not to exceed 100. It’s 6,000 tons, 140 meters in length, and therefore it was designed for North Atlantic operations, so it’s designed to operate in high sea states for long periods of time.” To field the platform in the U.S. fleet faster, the hull could be built abroad to the point where it’s ready to sail away while the combat system is integrated back in the U.S., Hine said. Another option is out of Spain’s Navantia, which is working on an export version of its Bonifaz-class F-110 anti-submarine warfare frigate. Navantia, which is partnered with Lockheed Martin for the F-110, plans to submit a bid should the U.S. Navy issue a request for proposals, Navantia commercial director Juan de la Cueva told USNI News during a wine and tapas-fueled reception on the convention center floor. F-110 frigate. Navantia image “All Navantia ships have a U.S. legacy because we came from a very long-standing relationship with the United States,” de la Cueva said. “We learned from Bath Iron Works, Gibbs & Cox how to build ships. So these ships pass … [Naval Sea Systems Command]” standards. De la Cueva noted the long relationship Navantia has maintained with major U.S. yards like General Dynamics Bath Iron Works and HII. The company has already provided the U.S. Navy with some information and is waiting to hear about the next steps in the competition. A U.S. variant could feature Lockheed Martin’s Aegis Combat System and the SPY-7 air and defense radar, de la Cueva said. In addition to the Brits and the Spanish, the Italians also have an option for the U.S. should it kick off an international competition. Italy’s Fincantieri, which has its own American subsidiary at Marinette Marine in Wisconsin, could propose the FREMM EVO. That platform is an updated version of the FREMM multi-mission frigate that the U.S. used as the parent design for the Constellation class. “I would call us untapped potential,” Fincantieri Marinette Marine chief executive officer George Moutafis told USNI News in September. The yard is still finishing the Royal Saudi Navy’s multi-mission surface combatant while building the first two Constellation-class frigates and preparing to build the Marine Corps’ Landing Ship Medium. “It’s an evolution of the original version, which is meant to say all the benefits are still there,” Moutafis said of the FREMM EVO. “The hard lines that work well for an [anti-submarine warfare] mission all is there, and they’ve been working on the areas that you would think would be the attractive ones – you know making it more lethal, making it ready to host energy-wise future growth for future missions, bringing in capabilities that have to do again with the ASW mission – and at the same time identifying the ways that it can integrate well with deploying, recovering and managing unmanned elements of across all domains.” The Wisconsin yard currently has about 2,200 employees and would need to hire about 500 over time should it receive a contract to build more frigates. Other possible designs could come out of Japan, South Korea and Turkey, USNI News previously reported . Following a discussion between Trump and Turkish leadership on the sidelines of July’s NATO summit, the Istanbul-class guided-missile frigate built by several Turkish shipyards entered the mix, two sources previously told USNI News. Fincantieri image Perhaps the nation most closely associated with the ongoing conversation about foreign shipbuilding is South Korea, which has pledged to invest $150 billion in the U.S. shipbuilding industry as part of a trade deal in the works with the Trump administration. The Chungnam-class guided-missile frigate, which several South Korean companies build, is one option under consideration, USNI News has learned. Meanwhile, the export version of Japan’s Mitsubishi Heavy Industries’ FFM Mogami-class guided-missile frigate is also on the table. While the Trump administration has repeatedly made its preference for an international competition known, the Navy has experienced setbacks when pursuing foreign designs. When altering the FREMM parent design for the Constellation-class program, Gibbs & Cox made so many changes to meet NAVSEA’s requirements that the commonality between the FREMM and the FFG(X) went from 85 percent to under 15 percent, USNI News reported in 2024 . “The thing that will prevent Constellation 2.0 is stop changing the requirement. If you set the requirement and leave it alone, and just let industry build it, whoever that is, that will stop Constellation 2.0,” Babcock’s Hine told USNI News. “Don’t even change the color of the curtains. Just build it,” he added. “It’s this sort of constant fiddling, and I know from being in the [U.K. Royal] Navy for most of my life, that we can’t help ourselves.”

title: Hong Kong 2019 protest prosecutions ‘no barrier’ to BN(O) visa route, UK home secretary confirms
zh_title: 英国内政大臣证实，2019 年香港抗议起诉对 BN(O) 签证途径“不构成障碍”
summary: 英国内政大臣证实，因参加 2019 年香港民主抗议活动而受到的起诉不会阻止其他符合资格的申请人获得英国国家（海外）签证途径。英国议会大厦，威斯敏斯特，伦敦。资料照片：Tom Grundy/HKFP。英国人权联合委员会寻求澄清，因为担心因与 2019 年示威和骚乱有关的罪行而被定罪的具有 BN(O) 身份的人可能会被拒绝入境或留下来。周三，内政大臣沙巴纳·马哈茂德回复了一封信
content:
英国内政大臣证实，因参加 2019 年香港民主抗议活动而受到的起诉不会阻止其他符合资格的申请人获得英国国家（海外）签证途径。英国议会大厦，威斯敏斯特，伦敦。资料照片：Tom Grundy/HKFP。英国人权联合委员会寻求澄清，因为担心因与 2019 年示威和骚乱有关的罪行而被定罪的具有 BN(O) 身份的人可能会被拒绝入境或留下来。周三，内政大臣沙巴纳·马哈茂德回复了委员会的一封信。她写道：“现在应该有一个假设，即确保与参加 2019 年抗议活动相关的定罪不会妨碍其他符合资格的个人从 BN(O) 路线中受益。因参加亲民主抗议活动而不符合标准 BN(O) 路线适用性要求的 BN(O) 路线申请人现在将自动被部长考虑在移民规则之外授予休假资格。”她补充说：“我感到自豪的是，英国已经为数千名香港人提供了安全港，政府将继续与香港人民站在一起。” 2019 年 12 月 8 日的抗议活动。照片：May James/HKFP。 2019 年 6 月，针对已被废除的引渡法案爆发了抗议活动。
在呼吁民主和对北京的侵犯感到愤怒的背景下，他们有时升级为对警察行为的暴力表达。示威者要求对警察行为进行独立调查，赦免被捕者，并停止将抗议活动定性为“骚乱”。  7月下旬，前民主党主席胡志伟抵达英国后在伦敦希思罗机场被拦截，在边境被拘留10小时后最初仅获得7天的移民保释。胡志伟在 2019 年的抗议活动中。照片：FTVV 截图。吴根据北京实施的国家安全法因阴谋颠覆国家而被定罪。他是被指控在 2020 年 7 月举行非官方民主立法会初选的 47 名民主党人之一。这位 63 岁的人被判入狱四年零五个月。英国当局后来批准他在该国居留六个月。已签发超过 230,000 份签证 人权联合委员会是一个议会小组，由来自下议院和上议院任命的 12 名成员组成。根据周三的新闻稿，人权联合委员会主席亚历克斯·索贝尔 (Alex Sobel) 表示：“BN(O) 路线的设立是专门为了确保英国能够成为那些因捍卫民主自由而受到不公正惩罚的人的庇护所。他们因参加抗议活动而被定罪，不应阻止人们参与这一计划。”
政府认识到这个问题并采取适当的行动来纠正它是正确的。”上周，英国表示，在英国的香港 BN(O) 签证持有者将不受一项将定居资格期限加倍至 10 年的提议的豁免。香港人的签证计划是在北京于 2020 年颁布香港国安法后推出的。据内政部称，截至今年 2 月，已有超过 23 万人获得了 BN(O) 签证，近 17 万人移居英国。北京于2020年6月将国家安全立法直接纳入香港小宪法

【原文 English Original】
Britain’s home secretary has confirmed that prosecutions for taking part in the 2019 pro-democracy protests in Hong Kong will not prevent otherwise eligible applicants from accessing the British National (Overseas) visa route. The UK Houses of Parliament, Westminster, London. File photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. The UK’s Joint Committee on Human Rights had sought the clarification amid concerns that people with BN(O) status convicted of offences connected to the 2019 demonstrations and unrest could be denied entry or leave to remain. On Wednesday, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood responded to a letter from the committee. She wrote: “[T]here should now be a presumption in favour of ensuring that convictions connected to participation in the 2019 protests do not prevent otherwise eligible individuals from benefiting from the BN(O) route. BN(O) route applicants who do not meet the standard BN(O) route suitability requirements due to participation in the pro-democracy protests will now be automatically considered by Ministers for a grant of leave outside the Immigration Rules.” “I am proud that the UK has already provided a safe haven to thousands of Hong Kongers and the Government will continue to stand with the people of Hong Kong,” she added. A protest on December 8, 2019. Photo: May James/HKFP. Protests erupted in June 2019 over a since-axed extradition bill . They escalated into sometimes violent displays of dissent against police behaviour, amid calls for democracy and anger over Beijing’s encroachment. Demonstrators demanded an independent probe into police conduct, amnesty for those arrested and a halt to the characterisation of protests as “riots.”  In late July, ex-Democratic Party chair Wu Chi-wai was stopped at London’s Heathrow Airport upon arriving in the UK and initially granted only seven days of immigration bail following a 10-hour detention at the border. Wu Chi-wai at the 2019 protests. Photo: FTVV screenshot. Wu was convicted under the Beijing-imposed national security law for conspiracy to subvert the state. He was among 47 democrats accused of holding an unofficial pro-democracy legislative primary election in July 2020. The 63-year-old was jailed for four years and five months. UK authorities later granted him leave to remain in the country for six months. Over 230,000 visas issued The Joint Committee on Human Rights is a parliamentary group of 12 members appointed from both the House of Commons and the House of Lords. According to a Wednesday press release, Chair of the Joint Committee on Human Rights Alex Sobel said: “The BN(O) route was set up specifically to ensure that the UK could be a place of sanctuary to those who were unjustly punished for standing up for their democratic freedoms. Convictions they received for taking part in the protests should not preclude people from accessing this scheme. It is right that the Government has recognised this issue and taken the appropriate action to remedy it.” Last week, the UK said Hong Kong BN(O) visa holders in the UK would be exempt from a proposal to double the qualifying period for settlement to 10 years. The visa scheme for Hongkongers was introduced following the 2020 enactment of the Beijing-imposed security law in the city. As of February this year, over 230,000 people had been granted a BN(O) visa and almost 170,000 had moved to the UK, according to the Home Office. Beijing inserted national security legislation directly into Hong Kong’s mini-constitution in June 2020 following a year of pro-democracy protests and unrest. It criminalised subversion, secession, collusion with foreign forces and terrorist acts – broadly defined to include disruption to transport and other infrastructure. The move gave police sweeping new powers and led to hundreds of arrests amid new legal precedents , while dozens of civil society groups disappeared . The authorities say it restored stability and peace to the city, rejecting criticism from trade partners , the UN and NGOs .

title: Nvidia preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang: US media
zh_title: 美媒：英伟达准备罢免CEO黄仁勋
summary: 美国媒体周三报道称，英伟达董事会正准备罢免其联合创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋，因为该芯片巨头的首席执行官在被曝与一名被指控为中国从事间谍活动的女性有染后，面临新的不忠指控。 Nvidia 创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋于 2026 年 1 月 5 日在内华达州拉斯维加斯举行的年度消费电子展之前，在 CES 2026 的 Nvidia Live 上发表讲话。照片：Patrick T. Fallon/法新社。据《华尔街日报》援引知情人士的消息称，该科技公司董事会正准备最快于周三召开会议，以确定黄的未来。
content:
美国媒体周三报道称，英伟达董事会正准备罢免其联合创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋，因为该芯片巨头的首席执行官在被曝与一名被指控为中国从事间谍活动的女性有染后，面临新的不忠指控。 Nvidia 创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋于 2026 年 1 月 5 日在内华达州拉斯维加斯举行的年度消费电子展之前，在 CES 2026 的 Nvidia Live 上发表讲话。照片：Patrick T. Fallon/法新社。据《华尔街日报》援引知情人士的话称，该科技公司董事会正准备最快于周三召开会议，以确定黄的未来。 《纽约时报》周三报道称，黄还与一名下属发生了第二次婚外情，称有视频证据显示这位 63 岁的高管与英伟达医疗保健副总裁金伯利·鲍威尔 (Kimberly Powell) 关系密切。据《泰晤士报》报道，48 岁的鲍威尔一直是英伟达努力将芯片技术扩展到高等教育和医疗保健领域的公开代言人，他在加利福尼亚州圣何塞举行的一次会议上发表了讲话，旁观者“看到他们在酒店里充满感情”。在报道第二起事件之前，黄承认与新加坡数据中心公司 Megaspeed 的高级管理人员 Alice Huang 存在关系。 《华尔街日报》报道称，两人曾于2024年和2025年在台北被拍到在一起。
Nvidia 创始人、总裁兼首席执行官黄仁勋于 2025 年 4 月 30 日在华盛顿特区举行的 2025 年 Hill & Valley 论坛上。照片：The Hill and Valley 论坛，来自 YouTube。据报道，美国情报部门去年春天散发了一份备忘录，指控黄爱丽是中国国家安全部的资产。这位英伟达首席执行官在周日给英伟达员工的一封信中承认与黄仁勋有关系——他与黄仁勋没有任何亲属关系——并写道：“我对我的妻子不忠。”同一天，英伟达董事会在一份声明中表示，他们“根据最近有关创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋成为外国情报工作目标的报道，启动了一项独立调查”。另请参阅：英伟达首席执行官事件再次推动美国对中国采取更强硬立场“我支持调查并将全力配合。我爱我们的国家和我们的公司，”黄在声明中写道。据《泰晤士报》报道，国会还要求他就他与爱丽丝黄的互动提供闭门简报。随着人工智能行业的蓬勃发展，英伟达的股价再创新高，黄仁勋在白宫活动中出现在美国总统唐纳德·特朗普身边，就在上个月，他接受了共和党领导人颁发的国家科学奖章。 2025 年 4 月 30 日星期三，在白宫十字厅举行的“投资美国”活动中，NVIDIA 首席执行官黄仁勋在唐纳德·特朗普总统的注视下发表讲话。
照片：白宫，来自 Flickr.Huang 是世界上最有影响力的科技领袖之一，其中包括埃隆·马斯克、杰夫·贝索斯和马克·扎克伯格，他们誓言要对人工智能进行自我监管，以应对可能的威胁，而特朗普拒绝了政府监管的呼吁，并驳回了该技术可能消灭人类的警告。英伟达股东对黄仁勋和这家人工智能芯片制造商提起集体诉讼，理由是他们未能向投资者披露有关双方关系的信息。自黄仁勋承认此事以来，英伟达股价近几天暴跌。 Nvidia 设计先进组件起源

【原文 English Original】
Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust its co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, US media reported Wednesday, as the chip giant’s chief faces new accusations of infidelity, after revelations he had an affair with a woman accused of spying for China. Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang speaks during Nvidia Live at CES 2026 ahead of the annual Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, Nevada, on January 5, 2026. Photo: Patrick T. Fallon/AFP. The tech company’s board was preparing to meet as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang’s future, according to the Wall Street Journal, which quoted people familiar with the matter. The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang was also involved in a second extramarital affair, with a subordinate, saying there was video evidence of the 63-year-old executive being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell. Powell, 48, has been a public face of Nvidia’s efforts to expand the chip technology into higher education and health care, and was speaking at a San Jose, California conference where they “were seen being affectionate at the hotel” by bystanders, the Times reported. The report of the second affair follows Huang’s acknowledgment of a relationship with Alice Huang, a senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. The Wall Street Journal reported that the two were photographed together in Taipei in 2024 and 2025. Nvidia founder, president and CEO Jensen Huang at the Hill & Valley Forum 2025 in Washington, DC, on April 30, 2025. Photo: The Hill and Valley Forum, via YouTube. US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this past spring alleging Alice Huang was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. The Nvidia CEO admitted to having had a relationship with Huang — to whom he bears no familial relation — in a note to Nvidia employees Sunday, writing: “I was unfaithful to my wife.” The same day Nvidia’s board of directors said in a statement that they’d launched “an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” See also: Nvidia CEO affair revives push for tougher US line on China “I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company,” Huang wrote in his statement. He has also been called on by Congress to provide a closed-door briefing on his interactions with Alice Huang, the Times reported. As the artificial intelligence industry surge has spurred Nvidia’s stock prices to new heights, Huang has appeared at US President Donald Trump’s side at White House events, as recently as last month when he accepted a National Medal of Science from the Republican leader. NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang delivers remarks as President Donald Trump looks on during an “Investing in America” event, Wednesday, April 30, 2025, in the Cross Hall of the White House. Photo: The White House, via Flickr. Huang was among the world’s most influential tech leaders — including Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos and Mark Zuckerberg — who vowed to self-regulate AI against possible threats, as Trump rejected calls for government oversight and dismissed warnings the technology could wipe out humanity. Nvidia shareholders filed a class action lawsuit against Huang and the AI chip maker for failing to disclose information about the relationship to investors. Nvidia shares have plummeted in recent days since Huang admitted to the affair. Nvidia designs advanced components originally created to handle 3D visuals in video games, called Graphics Processing Units (GPUs). Nvidia’s processors are mostly made by Taiwanese company TSMC, the world’s largest contract manufacturer of chips.

title: UPDATED: USS South Dakota Command Triad Relieved After October Grounding, Congressman Says
zh_title: 更新：国会议员称，十月搁浅后，南达科他州三合会指挥部被解职
summary: 2026 年 6 月 30 日，在康涅狄格州格罗顿的新伦敦海军潜艇基地，弗吉尼亚级核动力快速攻击潜艇南达科他号 (SSN-790) 指挥变更仪式上，鸣放 11 响礼炮，迎接第 2 潜艇大队指挥官梅尔文·史密斯少将的到来。丹尼尔·古德温接替了中校的职务。伯恩斯·C·W·布朗 (Burnes C.W. Brown) 担任南达科他州指挥官。美国海军照片 美国海军照片 南达科他号航空母舰 (SSN-790) 的指挥三合会上个月因搁浅事件而被拆除，根据一名国会议员的声明。潜艇的指挥官、执行官a
content:
2026 年 6 月 30 日，在康涅狄格州格罗顿的新伦敦海军潜艇基地，弗吉尼亚级核动力快速攻击潜艇南达科他号 (SSN-790) 指挥变更仪式上，鸣放 11 响礼炮，迎接第 2 潜艇大队指挥官梅尔文·史密斯少将的到来。丹尼尔·古德温接替了中校的职务。伯恩斯·C·W·布朗 (Burnes C.W. Brown) 担任南达科他州指挥官。美国海军照片 美国海军照片 南达科他号航空母舰 (SSN-790) 的指挥三合会上个月因搁浅事件而被拆除，根据一名国会议员的声明。根据众议院海上力量和投送部队小组委员会高级成员乔·考特尼（康涅狄格州民主党人）众议员和众议院军事委员会高级成员亚当·史密斯（华盛顿州民主党人）周四发布的一封信，该潜艇的指挥官、执行官和艇长于 10 月 14 日被解除指挥权，据称此次解除是由于搁浅事件。指挥官。据康涅狄格州新伦敦《每日报》报道，丹·古德温被解除南达科他州指挥官职务。根据五角大楼发布的消息，古德温于 2026 年 6 月接任南达科他州指挥官。一位知情人士告诉美国海军学院新闻，在潜艇舵软接地后，三合会被移除。信中称，议员们从一名记者要求对解雇事件发表评论的请求中得知，他们松了口气。
近一个月后，众议院军事委员会尚未收到任何有关解雇或潜在事件的通知。 2026 年 6 月 30 日在康涅狄格州格罗顿新伦敦海军潜艇基地的快速攻击潜艇码头上举行南达科他号 (SSN-790) 号航空母舰指挥变更仪式后，南达科他号 (SSN-790) 舰长丹尼尔·古德温被送上岸。信中写道：“海军部未能向国会通报这些事件是不可接受的。”致代理海军部长曹洪和海军作战部长达里尔·考德尔上将。海军通常会向国会通报海上事件、事故和指挥三合会的解散。 “海军缺乏透明度留下了许多悬而未决的问题，不仅涉及发生了什么，还涉及导致三合会解散的事件对南达科他州的结构健康、船员的福祉的影响，以及该事件是否暴露了必须解决的标准程序培训方面的任何系统性问题。由于海军未能沟通，本应成为信息共享标准的演习反而引发了人们对海军对透明度的承诺以及对与国会建立富有成效的工作关系的承诺的质疑。”这封信。一名国防官员向美国海军学院新闻证实了这一消息。
海军发言人承认了美国海军学院新闻的提问，但没有立即发表评论。 目前尚不清楚南达科他州是否受损。南达科他号于 2019 年服役，是海军最先进的潜艇之一，也是新型潜艇技术的试验台。美国海军学院新闻 2016 年报道称：“这艘船采用了使船舶更安静的涂层、更安静的喷水推进器以及安装在船体两侧的附加声纳，以提高船员探测敌方船只和潜艇的能力。”美国攻击潜艇上一次重大搁浅是在 2021 年。在南海执行任务时，美国海军康涅狄格号 (SSN-21) 与一艘水下潜艇相撞。

【原文 English Original】
11-gun salutes are fired for the arrival of Rear Adm. Melvin Smith, Commander, Submarine Group 2, during the Virginia-class nuclear-powered fast attack submarine USS South Dakota (SSN-790) Change of Command Ceremony at Naval Submarine Base New London in Groton, Connecticut, June 30, 2026. Cmdr. Daniel Goodwin relieved Cmdr. Burnes C.W. Brown as Commanding Officer of South Dakota. US Navy photo USS South Dakota (SSN-790) command triad was removed last month following a grounding incident, according to a statement from a member of Congress. The submarine’s commanding officer, executive officer and chief of the boat were relieved from command on Oct. 14, with the relief allegedly attributed to a grounding incident, according to a letter released Thursday by Reps. Joe Courtney (D-Conn.), Ranking Member of the House Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee, and Adam Smith (D-Wash.), Ranking Member of the House Armed Services Committee. Cmdr. Dan Goodwin was relieved as commander of South Dakota , according to a story in the Day newspaper based in New London, Conn. Goodwin assumed command of South Dakota in June of 2026, according to a Pentagon release . A source familiar told USNI News the triad removal followed a soft grounding of the submarine’s rudder. Lawmakers learned of the relief from a reporter’s request for comment on the dismissal, according to the letter. Nearly one month later, no notifications of the firings or the underlying incident had been made to the House Armed Services Committee. Cmdr. Daniel Goodwin, commanding officer of USS South Dakota (SSN-790) is piped ashore following the USS South Dakota (SSN-790) change of command ceremony that was held June 30, 2026, onboard the fast attack submarine pierside at Naval Submarine Base New London in Groton, Conn. US Navy photo “The Department of the Navy’s failure to communicate these incidents to Congress is unacceptable,” reads the letter, which is addressed to Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao and Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle. The Navy typically informs Congress of at-sea incidents, accidents and dismissals of command triads. “The Navy’s lack of transparency leave many outstanding questions about not only what occurred, but the impact of the events leading the triad’s dismissal on the structural health of South Dakota , the well-being of the crew, and whether the incident laid bare any systemic issues with training to standard procedures that must be addressed. As a result of the Navy’s failure to communicate, what should have been a standard exercise in information sharing has instead raised questions about the Navy’s commitment to transparency and its commitment to a productive working relationship with Congress,” reads the letter. A defense official confirmed the removals to USNI News. A Navy spokesperson acknowledged a question from USNI News but did not immediately provide a comment. It’s unclear whether South Dakota was damaged. Commissioned in 2019, South Dakota is one of the Navy’s most advanced submarines and serves as the test bed for new submarine technology. “The boat received coatings that keep the ship quieter, a quieter water jet propulsor and additional sonars mounted on the sides of the hull to increase the crew’s ability to detect enemy ships and submarines,” USNI News reported in 2016 . The last major grounding of a U.S. attack submarine was in 2021. While operating in the South China Sea, USS Connecticut (SSN-21) collided with an underwater sea mount, resulting in extensive damage to the boat. The submarine is still undergoing repairs.

title: Russia’s Push for AI Sovereignty Faces Setbacks
zh_title: 俄罗斯推动人工智能主权面临挫折
summary: 内容摘要：10 月份乌克兰无人机袭击俄罗斯，损坏了 Yandex、VK、Sberbank 和俄罗斯联邦税务局运营的数据中心，扰乱了数字服务，并引发了将基础设施从莫斯科地区搬迁到远东的讨论。随着人们越来越担心俄罗斯系统落后于美国和中国模式，莫斯科正在着手正式确定其人工智能（AI）政策。新的人工智能立法于 9 月生效。俄罗斯官员将国内人工智能视为国家主权问题，但计算基础设施和滑雪设备短缺
content:
内容摘要：10 月份乌克兰无人机袭击俄罗斯，损坏了 Yandex、VK、Sberbank 和俄罗斯联邦税务局运营的数据中心，扰乱了数字服务，并引发了将基础设施从莫斯科地区搬迁到远东的讨论。随着人们越来越担心俄罗斯系统落后于美国和中国模式，莫斯科正在着手正式确定其人工智能（AI）政策。新的人工智能立法于 9 月生效。俄罗斯官员将国内人工智能视为国家主权问题，但计算基础设施和技术人员的短缺，以及外国人工智能模型的日益使用，威胁着莫斯科发展有竞争力的国内行业的努力。 10 月 8 日，乌克兰无人机袭击了俄罗斯最大科技公司 Yandex 旗下的大型数据中心之一，导致该公司在全国各地的服务大规模中断。罢工使该公司的云服务进入紧急模式，客户不得不将数据转移到其他云系统（Habr，10 月 12 日）。 Yandex 数字生态系统内的其他服务需要数周时间才能恢复（T-J，10 月 26 日）。
VK Company Limited 是另一家控制着领先的俄语社交媒体网站 VKontakte 和 Odnoklassniki、国家消息系统 Max 以及俄罗斯领先的电子邮件服务 Mail.ru 的大型科技公司，最近其数据中心也遭受了损害，俄罗斯最大的金融机构 Sberbank 也是如此（CNews，10 月 18 日）。这些攻击只是克里姆林宫在继续推动完全数字主权时面临的众多困难之一。这些 10 月份的攻击符合乌克兰无人机针对俄罗斯数据中心的更广泛模式，包括那些属于联邦组织的数据中心，例如下诺夫哥罗德的国家税务局（Nastoyashee Vremya，10 月 23 日）。 Ozon 是一家电子商务公司，被认为是俄罗斯的亚马逊，自 8 月以来一直面临着针对其仓库的无人机袭击（Omskinform，10 月 28 日）。这些攻击对俄罗斯发展安全和主权科技行业的努力产生了严重后果。俄罗斯科技行业正在呼吁加强安全性，一些人正在讨论将数据中心迁往远东的可能性，因为目前 75% 的商业数据中心位于莫斯科州（Techora，10 月 27 日）。技术媒体讨论的其他选择包括将数据中心移至哈萨克斯坦。 Yandex 尚未面临西方的全面制裁，使其有可能将基础设施转移到国外（Habr，10 月 12 日）。
对俄罗斯科技行业的物理攻击正值克里姆林宫越来越担心该国人工智能（AI）的未来。俄罗斯杜马成立了一个委员会来解决人工智能问题，由执政的统一俄罗斯党副秘书长、俄罗斯“外国代理人”法的发起人之一亚历山大·西迪亚金（Aleksandr Sidyakin）领导，该法名义上旨在减少外国在该国的影响力，并压制独立媒体、非政府组织和非系统性政治反对派（Meduza， 9 月 24 日）。俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京表示，俄罗斯的主权将取决于该国开发自己的国内人工智能的能力（RBC，4 月 10 日）。人工智能在俄罗斯对乌克兰战争中的快速发展彻底改变了战场，减少了
