资助机会通知 (NOFO)：在斯威士兰举办 2027 GCTF 研讨会 资助机会通知 (NOFO) 在斯威士兰美国台湾学院举办 2027 G CTF 研讨会 机会编号：GCTF-TAIPEI-FY2 7 -00 1 申请截止日期：202 年 11 月 23 日 6 日晚上 11:59 （台北时间） A. 基本信息 1. 概述 资助方式：合作协议。合作协议包括局或大使馆实质性参与项目的计划实施。下文 C.2 节包含实质性参与的示例。项目实施期限：拟建项目应于202年5月31日前完成 7．本通知视资金情况而定。公共外交部门保留在被认为符合美国政府最佳利益的情况下授予少于或超过所述资金的权利，具体取决于资金的可用性和指定拨款官员的批准。 2. 执行摘要 美国在台协会 (AIT) 公共外交部门 (PDS) 宣布开展一项合作协议公开竞赛，以支持 2027 年第一季度或第二季度在斯威士兰规划和实施全球合作与培训框架 (GCTF) 区域特许经营研讨会。在资金允许的情况下，AIT 打算授予一份约 20 万美元的合作协议来实施该计划。
全球合作与培训框架（GCTF）是一个国际能力建设平台，汇集了政府官员、技术专家、行业代表、学者和民间社会代表，交流实践经验并加强应对区域和全球挑战的合作。GCTF由台湾和美国于2015年成立，此后扩大到包括日本、澳大利亚、加拿大和英国作为合作伙伴。拟议的研讨会“加强南部非洲的网络安全和数字治理”预计将于 2027 年第一季度或第二季度在斯威士兰举行。该计划将重点关注加强网络安全弹性、改善数字治理、保护关键数字基础设施、应对新出现的网络威胁以及促进安全和可信的数字转型。它将为参与者提供一个交流实践经验、确定共同挑战、加强专业网络和区域合作的平台。该研讨会预计将包括来自至少八个非洲国家的代表，特别强调南部非洲的区域参与。第一天预计将有约 60 至 80 名参与者参加，活动内容包括全体讨论、专家演讲和实践交流。
预计第二天将有约 40 名参与者参加，其中可能包括重点技术讨论、互动练习、工作组会议和/或相关现场参观。该计划预计将汇集来自参与非洲国家的政府官员、网络安全和数字治理从业者、技术专家、私营部门代表、学者、民间社会代表和其他相关利益攸关方。来自美国、台湾和其他 GCTF 合作伙伴（包括日本、澳大利亚、加拿大）的主题专家

【原文 English Original】
Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO): Implementation of 2027 GCTF Workshop in Eswatini Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) Implementation of 2027 G CTF Workshop in Eswatini American Institute in Taiwan Opportunity number: GCTF-TAIPEI-FY2 7 -00 1 Application deadline: November 23 , 202 6 , at 11:59 p.m. (Taipei Time)   A. Basic Information 1. Overview Funding Instrument Type: C ooperative agreement . Cooperative agreements include substantial involvement of the bureau or embassy in program implementation of the project. Examples of substantial involvement are included in section C.2 below. Project Performance Period : Proposed projects should be completed by May 31 , 202 7 . This notice is subject to availability of funding. The Public Diplomacy Section reserves the right to award less or more than the funds described under circumstances deemed to be in the best interest of the U.S. government, pending the availability of funds and approval of the designated grants officer. 2. Executive Summary The American Institute in Taiwan (AIT) Public Diplomacy Section (PDS) announces an open competition for a cooperative agreement to support the planning and implementation of a Global Cooperation and Training Framework (GCTF) regional franchise workshop in Eswatini in the first or second quarter of 2027. Subject to the availability of funding, AIT intends to award one cooperative agreement of approximately USD 200,000 to implement this program. The Global Cooperation and Training Framework (GCTF) is an international capacity-building platform that brings together government officials, technical experts, industry representatives, academics, and civil society representatives to exchange practical experiences and strengthen cooperation in addressing regional and global challenges. The GCTF was established by Taiwan and the United States in 2015 and has since expanded to include Japan, Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom as Partners. The proposed workshop, “Strengthening Cybersecurity and Digital Governance in Southern Africa,” is expected to take place in Eswatini during the first or second quarter of 2027. The program will focus on strengthening cybersecurity resilience, improving digital governance, protecting critical digital infrastructure, addressing emerging cyber threats, and promoting secure and trusted digital transformation. It will provide a platform for participants to exchange practical experiences, identify common challenges, and strengthen professional networks and regional cooperation. The workshop is expected to include representatives from at least eight African countries, with a particular emphasis on regional participation from Southern Africa. Approximately 60 to 80 participants are expected to participate in the first day of the program, which will feature plenary discussions, expert presentations, and practical exchanges. A smaller group of approximately 40 participants is expected to participate in the second day, which may include focused technical discussions, interactive exercises, working-group sessions, and/or relevant site visits. The program is expected to bring together government officials, cybersecurity and digital governance practitioners, technical experts, private-sector representatives, academics, civil society representatives, and other relevant stakeholders from participating African countries. Subject-matter experts from the United States, Taiwan, and other GCTF Partners, including Japan, Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom, may also be invited to contribute relevant international expertise and practical experience. The selected recipient will serve as AIT’s implementation partner and will be responsible for comprehensive program and logistical support, including venue and lodging coordination, participant management, travel arrangements for designated participants and speakers, ground transportation, interpretation and audiovisual services, workshop materials, vendor coordination, monitoring and evaluation, and required grant reporting. Travel expenses for U.S. Government officials invited by the U.S. Government and Taiwan-supported speakers will be funded separately and should not be included in the recipient’s proposed budget. AIT and GCTF partners will provide overall policy guidance, strategic direction, and substantive oversight throughout program planning and implementation. Eligible applicants include nonprofit organizations, educational institutions, professional associations, think tanks, private-sector organizations with relevant international program management experience, public international organizations where eligible under applicable U.S. Government regulations, and other eligible organizations with demonstrated capacity to organize international conferences or capacity-building programs and administer U.S. Government assistance awards. This cooperative agreement is intended to strengthen practical cybersecurity capacity and digital governance cooperation in Southern Africa, expand professional and institutional connections among participating countries, and advance the GCTF as a platform for practical international capacity building, technical exchange, and sustained regional cooperation. B. Eligibility 1. Eligible Applicants The following organizations are eligible to apply: Not-for-profit organizations , including non-governmental organizations (NGOs), think tanks, and civil society organizations Educational institutions , including universities and research institutions Professional associations and nonprofit organizations with demonstrated experience managing international conferences or capacity-building programs Private-sector organizations with demonstrated experience organizing international conferences or implementing international exchange programs Public international organizations , where eligible under applicable U.S. Government regulations Organizations may sub-contract with other entities, but only one entity, from the eligible categories of organizations listed above, can be the prime recipient of the award. When sub-contracting with other entities, the responsibilities of each entity must be clearly defined in the proposal. For more information on the difference between sub-contract and sub-recipient, please refer to 2 CFR 200 .331 . 2. Cost Sharing or Matching Cost sharing is not required . 3. Other Eligibility Requirements All organizations must have a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) issued via SAM.gov as well as a valid registration in SAM.gov. Please see Section D.3 for more information. Individuals are not required to have a UEI or be registered in SAM.gov. Applicants are only allowed to submit one proposal per organization. If more than one proposal is submitted from an organization, all proposals from that institution will be considered ineligible for funding. 4. This opportunity will not support: Projects relating to partisan political activity; Charitable or development activities; including direct social services such as medical, psychological, and/or humanitarian support Construction projects; Projects that support specific religious activities; Fund-raising campaigns; Lobbying for specific legislation or programs Scientific research or surveys; Commercial projects; Projects intended primarily for the growth or institutional development of the organization; Projects that duplicate existing projects; Illegal activities C. Program Description 1. Project Background, Goals, and Objectives Project Background The Global Cooperation and Training Framework (GCTF) is an international capacity-building platform established by Taiwan and the United States in 2015. Japan joined as a full partner in 2019, followed by Australia in 2021, Canada in 2023, and the United Kingdom in 2025. Through workshops and other capacity-building activities, GCTF brings together government officials, technical experts, industry representatives, and civil society representatives to exchange practical experience, strengthen professional networks, and develop approaches to shared regional and global challenges. As governments and societies become increasingly dependent on digital technologies and interconnected systems, cybersecurity and effective digital governance have become important elements of economic development, public-service delivery, critical infrastructure resilience, and public trust. Recent research documents that scam syndicates displaced from Southeast Asian epicenters, including Myanmar, Laos, and Cambodia, are actively pivoting to Africa, with documented raids in nine African countries and growing evidence of scam infrastructure, including online gambling platforms used as cover for fraud operations, gray business Telegram groups openly advertising scam facilities, and unregulated cryptocurrency services establishing footholds across the continent. Countries across Southern Africa face evolving cybersecurity and cybercrime challenges while also seeking to expand digital services, strengthen institutional capacity, and develop governance frameworks that support secure and trusted digital transformation. The proposed GCTF regional workshop in Eswatini will provide a platform for government officials, cybersecurity and the digital governance practitioners, technical experts, private-sector representatives, academics, civil society representatives, and other relevant stakeholders from across Africa to exchange practical experiences and strengthen professional and institutional connections. The workshop is expected to include representatives from at least eight African countries, with particular emphasis on participation from Southern Africa. The program will draw on expertise and practical experience from participating African countries as well as the United States, Taiwan, and other GCTF partners, as appropriate. Through expert presentations, policy and technical discussions, interactive exchanges, and other practical activities, the workshop will address shared challenges and identify approaches that participating countries may adapt to their respective national and institutional contexts. Strengthening cybersecurity capacity and secure digital governance in Southern Africa also advances U.S. security and economic interests. Cyber threats, cyber-enabled crime, and vulnerabilities in interconnected digital systems increasingly cross-national borders and can affect American citizens, businesses, and critical infrastructure. By strengthening the ability of partner countries to prevent, identify, respond to, and recover from cyber threats, this program can help reduce vulnerabilities that may be exploited by transnational criminal networks and other malicious cyber actors. The workshop will also strengthen U.S. engagement with African partners on secure and resilient digital ecosystems, promote cooperation and information sharing among governments and technical experts, and expand relationships between African stakeholders and the United States and other GCTF partners. Through practical capacity building and sustained professional networks, the program will support a more secure and resilient regional digital environment while advancing shared interests in cybersecurity, economic security, and trusted digital development. Project Goal: The goal of this project is to strengthen cybersecurity resilience and digital governance capacity in Southern Africa by facilitating practical knowledge exchange, regional cooperation, and sustained professional engagement among participating countries and international partners, while advancing shared U.S. and partner interests in a more secure, resilient, and trusted digital environment. Project Objectives: The project will pursue the following objectives: Strengthen Cybersecurity Capacity and Resilience: Enhance participants’ knowledge of practical approaches to preventing, preparing for, responding to, and recovering from cybersecurity threats and incidents, with a specific focus on basic cyber hygiene, national cyber resilience, digital trust, and the development of a secure digital ecosystem aligned with global standards and best practices. Advance Effective and Secure Digital Governance: Promote the exchange of policies, practices, institutional approaches, and lessons learned that support secure, trusted, resilient, and inclusive digital governance and digital transformation. Promote Regional Cooperation and Information Sharing: Strengthen professional and institutional connections among participating African countries and encourage greater cross-border cooperation, information sharing, and coordination in addressing shared cybersecurity and digital governance challenges. Facilitate Practical International Exchange: Connect African policymakers and practitioners with relevant expertise and practical experience from participating African countries, the United States, Taiwan, and other GCTF partner countries, including Japan, Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom, as appropriate to the workshop agenda. Support Sustainable Professional Networks and Follow-on Cooperation: Encourage participants to identify practical opportunities for continued professional engagement, knowledge sharing, and future cooperation beyond the workshop. 2. Substantial Involvement This award will require substantial involvement from the American Institute in Taiwan (AIT ) and the U . S . Embassy in Eswatini . AIT will approve all key aspects of the workshop, including but not limited to venue selection, flight and hotel arrangements, ground transportation, lodging, visual designs, agenda, site visit locations, speaker and participant lists, catering and menus, conference room layout, lighting, and audio-visual setup. D. Application Contents and Format Please follow all instructions below carefully. Proposals that do not meet the requirements of this announcement or fail to comply with the stated requirements will be ineligible. Content of Application Please ensure: The proposal clearly addresses the goals and objectives of this funding opportunity All documents are in English All budgets are in U.S. dollars All pages are numbered, including budgets and attachments All documents are formatted to fit 8 ½ x 11 paper All documents are single-spaced, 14-point New Times Roman font, with 1-inch margins. Captions and footnotes may be 10-point New Times Roman font. Font sizes in charts and tables, including the budget, can be reformatted to fit within 1 page width. All applicant authorized signatures are provided where indicated on the various, required forms. The following documents are required: 1. Mandatory application forms SF-424 (Application for Federal Assistance – organizations) at https://grants.gov/ or https://www.ait.org.tw / . SF-424A (Budget Information for Non-Construction programs) at https://grants.gov/ or https://www.ait.org.tw / . SF-424B (Assurances for Non-Construction programs) at https://grants.gov/ or https://www.ait.org.tw / . (note: the SF-424B is only required for individuals, organizations exempt from registration, and for organizations not required to fully register in https://sam.gov/ ) 2. Proposal (10 pages maximum) The proposal should contain sufficient information that anyone not familiar with it would understand exactly what the applicant wants to do. You may use your own proposal format, but it must include all the items below. Proposal Summary: Short narrative that outlines the proposed project, including project objectives and anticipated impact. (Attachment: Recommended Proposal Template ). Introduction to the Organization : A description of past and present operations, showing ability to carry out the program, including information on all previous grants from the State Department and/or U.S. government agencies as well as experience with and expertise in areas related to those described in the NOFO. Applicants are encouraged, but not required, to use the attached Applicant Organization Information Survey form to provide this information (Attachment : Recommended Applicant Organization Information (AOI) Survey Template ). If the applicant chooses not to use the attached form, all of the requested information from the form will still need to be addressed in the application package. Problem Statement: Clear, concise and well-supported statement of the problem to be addressed and why the proposed program is needed Program Methods, Design, Activities, and Deliverables: The “goals” describe what the program is intended to achieve. The “objectives” refer to the intermediate accomplishments on the way to the goals. These should be achievable and measurable. Describe the program activities and how they will help achieve the objectives. Proposed Project Schedule and Timeline: The proposed timeline for the program activities. Include the dates, times, and locations of planned activities and events. Key Personnel: Names, titles, roles and experience/qualifications of key personnel involved in the program. What proportion of their time will be used in support of this program? Project Partners: List the names and type of involvement of key partner organizations and sub-awardees (if applicable). Future Funding or Sustainability: Applicant’s plan for continuing the program beyond the grant period, or the availability of other resources, if applicable. Monitoring & Evaluation Plan: Proposals must include a draft Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Performance Monitoring Plan (PMP). The M&E PMP should show how applicants intend to measure and demonstrate progress towards the project’s objectives and goals. The key components to the PMP are as follows: Monitoring and Evaluation Narrative: In narrative form, applicants should describe how they intend to monitor and evaluate the activities of their award. In addition, the applicant should describe any M&E processes, including key personnel, management structure (where M&E fits into the overall program’s staff structure), technology, and as well provide a brief budget narrative explaining any line-item expenditures for M&E listed in the program’s budget. If the proposal is from a prior grantee, the proposal discusses how the grantee has adapted, improved or otherwise modified their approach based on learning from previous experience. This narrative is limited to two pages. Theory of Change Diagram: Applicants are expected to submit either a Theory of Change diagram or an If-Then Statement that illustrates how project activities will lead to intended outcomes. Monitoring and Evaluation Datasheet: The applicant must include their proposed activities and their expected outputs and outcomes as well as the goals and objectives as written in the NOFO. The datasheet’s purpose is to explicitly illustrate how a project’s activities lead to tangible results (such as increased beneficiary skills, knowledge, or attitudes) that ultimately address a PDS objective. The selected applicant’s M&E PMP is subject to review and approval before any award will be issued under this NOFO. The selected applicant will be required to work with the Public Diplomacy Section’s Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist to ensure the applicant’s M&E PMP achieves an expected level of expertise and meets PDS objectives. Expenses directly associated with monitoring and evaluation are considered allowable. The suggested template includes a space to list the portion of the total budget amount directly associated with monitoring and evaluation activities. 3. Budget Justification Narrative Detailed Budget – Applicants must submit a detailed line-item budget. Applicants are encouraged to utilize the template provided with the funding opportunity but are not required to do so (Attachment: Recommended Budget Narrative Template ). Line-item expenditures should be listed in the greatest possible detail. The budget must identify the total amount of funding requested, with a breakdown of amounts to be spent in the following budget categories: personnel; fringe benefits; travel; equipment; supplies; consultants/contracts; other direct costs; and indirect costs. See Annex Section I for a description of the types of costs that should be included in each category. Personnel salaries should include the level of effort and the rate of pay, which should cover the percentage of time each staff member will dedicate to grant-based activities. If an organization is charging an indirect cost rate without a NICRA, it must apply it to the modified total budget costs (MTDC), refer to 2CFR § 200.1 . Budgets shall be submitted in U.S. dollars and final grant agreements will be conducted in U.S. dollars. Budget Justification Narrative – Applicants must submit a budget justification narrative to accompany the detailed line-item budget. The purpose of the budget justification narrative is to supplement the information provided in the detailed budget spreadsheet by justifying how the budget cost elements are necessary to implement project objectives and accomplish the project goals. The budget justification narrative is a tool to help AIT staff fully understand the budgetary needs of the applicant and is an opportunity to provide descriptive information about the requested costs beyond the constraints of the budget template. Together, the detailed budget spreadsheet, the budget justification narrative, and the SF-424A should provide a complete financial and qualitative description that supports the proposed project plan and should be directly relatable to the specific project components described in the applicant’s proposal. Additional Budget Notes: Curing venues, managing logistics, catering, etc. are allowable. Audit Requirements: Please note the audit requirements for Department of State awards in the Standard Terms and Conditions https://www.state.gov/federal-assistance-policies-appeals, Subpart F – Audit Requirements. The cost of the required audits may be charged either as an allowable direct cost to the award OR included in the organization’s established indirect costs in the award’s detailed budget. Visa Fees: Include all visa application and related fees in your budget as applicable. Please note DS-2019s for post-funded programs must be submitted directly by the award recipient. If you anticipate your program will include the DS-2019 visa processing, your organization must be a registered Designated Sponsoring Organization. For more information go to: https://j1visa.state.gov/sponsors/become-a-sponsor/ 4. Attachments Key Personnel Resumes : A résumé, not to exceed one page in length, must be included for the proposed key staff persons, such as the Project Director and Finance Officer, as well as any speakers or trainers (if applicable). If an individual for this type of position has not been identified, the applicant may submit a 1-page position description, identifying the qualifications and skills required for that position, in lieu of a résumé. Letters of support from program partners: Letters of support should be included for sub-recipients or other partners. The letters must identify the type of relationship to be entered into (formal or informal), the roles and responsibilities of each partner in relation to the proposed project activities, and the expected result of the partnership. The individual letters cannot exceed 1 page in length. Indirect Costs : If your organization has a Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (NICRA) and includes NICRA charges in the budget, your latest NICRA should be included in the application submission. Proof of Non-profit Status: Documentation to demonstrate the applicant’s non-profit status (e.g., U.S.-based organizations should submit a copy of their 501(c)(3) Internal Revenue Service determination letter, and non-U.S. organizations should provide evidence of non-profit status issued by a government entity). Proof of Registration: A copy of the organization’s registration should be provided with the proposal application. U.S.-based organizations should submit a copy of their IRS determination letter. Taiwan -based organizations should submit a copy of their certificate of registration from the appropriate government organization. Other items NOT required/requested with the application submission, but which may be requested if your application is approved to move forward in the review process include: Copies of an organization or program audit within the last two (2) years Copies of relevant human resources, financial, or procurement policies Copies of other relevant organizational policies or documentation that would help the Department determine your organization’s capacity to manage a federal grant award overseas Documentation that demonstrates the recipients’ plan and/or policy to safeguard PII of participants and beneficiaries. It is the responsibility of the recipient to ensure protection of personally identifiable information (PII) and safeguard PII when collecting, maintaining, using and disseminating such information Information to determine what financial controls and standard operating procedures an organization uses to procure goods and services, hire staff and track time and attendance, pay for grant-related travel, and identify other financial transactions that may be necessary to undertake the project activities AIT reserves the right to request any additional programmatic and/or financial information regarding the proposal. E. Submission Requirements and Deadlines 1.Address to Request Application Package Application forms required above are available at https://www.ait.org.tw/ , grants.gov, MyGrants, etc. 2.Department of State Contacts If you have any questions about the grant application process, please contact: AITGCTF@state.gov . Question Deadline: For questions on this solicitation, please contact AITGCTF@state.gov . Questions must be received before October 28, 2026 , at 23:59 p.m. (Taipei Time) . Applicants should not expect an email response to questions, as questions received before the deadline will be answered in a question-and-answer document and posted at http://www.grants.gov and https://www.ait.org.tw/ . 3.Unique entity identifier and System for Award Management (SAM.gov) Required Registration: All organizations, whether based in the United States or in another country, must have a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and an active registration in SAM.gov. A UEI is one of the data elements mandated by Public Law 109-282, the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act (FFATA), for all Federal awards. An applicant must maintain an active registration while it has a proposal under review by the Department and must continue to keep the registration active for the entire duration of the period of performance of any Federal award that results from this NOFO. The 2 CFR 200 also requires subrecipients to obtain a UEI. Please note the UEI for subrecipients is not required at the time of application but will be required before an award is processed and/or directed to a subrecipient. Note: The process of obtaining or renewing a SAM.gov registration may take anywhere from 4-8 weeks. Please begin your registration as early as possible . Organizations based in the United States or that pay employees within the United States will need an Employer Identification Number (EIN) from the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and a UEI prior to registering in SAM.gov. Organizations based outside of the United States and that do not pay employees within the United States do not need an EIN from the IRS but do need a UEI prior to registering in SAM.gov. Organizations based outside of the United States that do not intend to apply for U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) awards are no longer required to have a NATO Commercial and Government Entity (NCAGE) code to apply for non-DoD foreign assistance funding opportunities. If an applicant organization is mid-registration and wishes to remove an NCAGE code from their SAM.gov registration, the applicant should submit a help desk ticket (“incident”) with the Federal Service Desk (FSD) online at www.fsd.gov using the following language: “I do not intend to seek financial assistance from the Department of Defense. I do not wish to obtain an NCAGE code. I understand that I will need to submit my registration after this incident is resolved in order to have my registration activated.” Organizations based outside of the United States and that DO NOT plan to do business with the DoD should follow the below instructions: Step 1: Proceed to SAM.gov to obtain a UEI and complete the SAM.gov registration process. SAM.gov registration must be renewed annually. Exemptions An exemption from the UEI and sam.gov registration requirements may be permitted on a case-by-case basis. See 2 CFR 25.110 for a full list of exemptions. Organizations requesting exemption from UEI or SAM.gov requirements must email the point of contact listed in the NOFO at least two weeks prior to the deadline in the NOFO providing a justification of their request. Approval for a SAM.gov exemption must come from the warranted Grants Officer before the application can be deemed eligible for review. Please note : Any applicant with an exclusion in the System for Award Management (SAM) is not eligible to apply for an assistance award in accordance with the OMB guidelines at 2 CFR 180 that implement Executive Orders 12549 (3 CFR, 1986 Comp., p. 189) and 12689 (3 CFR, 1989 Comp., p. 235), “Debarment and Suspension.”   4.Submission Dates and Times Submission Deadline: All applications must be received by November 23 , 2026 , at 23:59 p.m. ( Taipei Time ) . For the purposes of determining if an award is submitted on time, PDS will utilize the timestamp provided by MyGrants or Grants.gov. This deadline is firm and is not a rolling deadline. If organizations fail to meet the deadline noted above their application will be considered ineligible and will not be considered for funding. Applicants using MyGrants for the first time will need their “New Organization Registration.” To register with MyGrants, navigate to https://MyGrants.servicenowservices.com and click “Create an Account” under “New User?” On the pop-up select “Create a MyGrants Applicant/Grantee Account” and complete all required fields. Once completed, an email will be sent to verify the account creation followed by an Okta Account set-up which will require the use of a smartphone for multi-factor authentication (MFA). If an applicant does not have accessibility to a smartphone during the time of account creation, please contact the helpdesk. MyGrants Help Desk: For assistance with MyGrants accounts and technical issues related to the system, please contact the ILMS help desk by phone at +1 (888) 313-4567 (toll charges apply for international callers) or through the Self Service online portal that can be accessed from ILMS Self Service Portal. Customer support is available 24/7. See https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/pay-leave/federal-holidays/ for a list of federal holidays. Grants.gov Helpdesk: For assistance with Grants.gov, please call the Contact Center at +1 (800) 518-4726 or email support@grants.gov . The Contact Center is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week, except federal holidays. See https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/pay-leave/federal-holidays/ for a list of federal holidays. Submission Method : Submitting all application materials directly to the following email address: AITGCTF@state.gov . Applicants must include the Funding Opportunity Title and Funding Opportunity Number in the subject line of the email. 5.Funding Restrictions i. Funding Restrictions for the United Nations Relief and Works Agency (UNRWA): None of the funds awarded resulting from this Notice of Funding Opportunity may be made available for subawards, direct financial support, or otherwise used to provide any payment or transfer to United Nations Relief and Works Agency (UNRWA). ii. Certification Regarding Compliance with Applicable Federal Anti-Discrimination Laws” If the place of performance or delivery of any award made under this NOFO will be within the United States, applicants are advised that they will be required to certify the following at the time of award: a. Its compliance in all respects with all applicable Federal anti-discrimination laws is material to the government’s payment decisions for purposes of section 3729(b)(4) of title 31, United States Code and; b. It does not operate any programs promoting Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion that violate any applicable Federal anti-discrimination laws. A program promoting Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion means a program whose purpose is to promote preferences based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origins, such as in training or hiring. iii. Certification of Trafficking in Persons Compliance and Compliance Plan: Applicants are advised that they will be required to certify the following at the time of award for awards where the estimated value of services to be performed outside the United States exceeds $500,000: To the best of the Recipient’s knowledge, neither the Recipient, nor any subrecipient, contractor, or subcontractor of the Recipient or any agent of the recipient or of such a subrecipient, contractor, or subcontractor, is engaged in any of the activities described in 2 CFR 175.105(a); The recipient has implemented a Trafficking in Persons compliance plan to prevent activities described in 2 CFR 175(a) and is compliant with this plan; and the compliance plan must follow the minimum requirements described in 2 CFR 175(b)(5). That the Recipient has and will implement procedures to prevent activities described in 2 CFR 175.105(a) and to monitor, detect, and terminate any subrecipient, contractor, subcontractor, or employee of the recipient engaging in these activities. https://fsapartners.ed.gov/knowledge-center/topics/section-117-foreign-gift-and-contract-reporting/resources/frequently-asked-questions Recipients do not need to submit a copy of the plan. However, they must provide it to the Grants Officer upon request, and as appropriate, must post the useful and relevant contents of the plan or related materials on its website and at the workplace. Recipients must re-certify on an annual basis for the entire award period of performance. iv. Prohibition on Unmanned Aircraft Systems Manufactured or Assembled by American Security Drone Act-Covered Foreign Entities (a) Definitions. American Security Drone Act-covered foreign entity means an entity included on a list developed and maintained by the Federal Acquisition Security Council (FASC) and published in the System for Award Management (SAM) at https://www.sam.gov FASC-prohibited unmanned aircraft system means an unmanned aircraft system manufactured or assembled by an American Security Drone Act-covered foreign entity. Unmanned aircraft means an aircraft that is operated without the possibility of direct human intervention from within or on the aircraft. Unmanned aircraft system means an unmanned aircraft and associated elements (including communication links and the components that control the unmanned aircraft) that are required for the operator to operate safely and efficiently in the national airspace system. (b) Prohibition. Recipients of funding under this Notice of Funding Opportunity (including subawards and subcontracts issued by the recipient) will be prohibited from: Delivering any FASC-prohibited unmanned aircraft system, which includes unmanned aircraft (i.e., drones) and associated elements; Operating a FASC-prohibited unmanned aircraft system in the performance of the award; and Using Federal funds for the purchase or operation of a FASC-prohibited unmanned aircraft system. (c) Exemptions, exceptions, and waivers. The prohibitions described above will not apply if the agency determines that an exemption, exception, or waiver applies and the award indicates that such a determination has been made. [See sections 1823 through 1825 and 1832 of Public Law 118-31 ( 41 U.S.C. 3901 note prec.) for statutory requirements pertaining to exemptions, exceptions, and waivers.]. v. Promoting Human Flourishing in Foreign Assistance (PHFFA) Applicants for foreign assistance awards should be aware of requirements in 2 CFR Part 602, 603, and 604. These policies are referred to collectively as the Promoting Human Flourishing in Foreign Assistance (PHFFA) Policy. 602 : The award term imposes certain abortion-related requirements on foreign nongovernmental organizations (NGOs), United States NGOs, public international organizations, foreign governments, and parastatals. 603 : The award term imposes certain requirements relating to gender ideology on foreign nongovernmental organizations (NGOs), United States NGOs, international organizations, foreign governments, and parastatals. 604 : The award term imposes certain requirements relating to discriminatory equity ideology on foreign nongovernmental organizations (NGOs), United States NGOs, international organizations, foreign governments, and parastatals. The Department recognizes there are costs associated with these policies. Potential one-time and recurring costs the Department identifies for recipients and grantees are for familiarization with the policy, development and delivery of organizational training and implementation guidance, routine compliance monitoring, and recordkeeping and reporting requirements. Vi. Pre-Award Costs : Pre-award costs are not an allowable expense for this funding opportunity. Vii. Construction : Any award made as a result of this NOFO will not allow for construction activities or costs. Viii. Direct Social Services: Costs that cover and provide direct social services, such as welfare, charity, health or economic relief, are unallowable. Medical assistance, such as costs to include medical professionals, including but not limited to doctors, nurses, and psychiatrists to participate in the project activities are not allowed. 6.Copyrights and Proprietary Information If any of the information contained in your application is proprietary, please note in the footer of the appropriate pages that the information is Confidential – Proprietary. Applicants should also note what parts of the application, program, concept, etc. are covered by copyright(s), trademark(s), or any other intellectual property rights and provide copies of the relevant documentation to support these copyrights. Applicants must acquire all required registrations and rights in the United States and Taiwan. All intellectual property considerations and rights must be fully met in the United States and Taiwan. Any sub-recipient organization must also meet all the U.S. and Taiwan requirements described above.   F. Application Review Information 1. Review Criteria Criteria: Each application submitted under this announcement will be evaluated and rated on the basis of the criteria enumerated below. The criteria are designed to assess the quality of the proposed project, and to determine the likelihood of its success. Quality and Feasibility of the Program Idea – 20 points: The program idea should be innovative and well developed, with sufficient detail about how p roject activities will be carried out. The proposals should demonstrate originality and outline clear, achievable objectives that align directly with the priorities and requirements of the NOFO . The proposal includes a reasonable implementation timeline, and the project scope is appropriate and clearly defined. Finally, the proposal aligns with the following: The project clearly demonstrates a direct contribution to current U.S. foreign policy priorities. The project will positively impact America’s reputation among foreign government partners. The project will positively impact American’s reputation among foreign publics. The proposal does not include any activities contrary to the following Executive Orders: Executive Order 14173: “Ending Illegal Discrimination and Restoring Merit-Based Opportunity Executive Order 14287: “Protecting American Communities from Criminal Aliens” Executive Order 14168: Defending Women from Gender Ideology Extremism and Restoring Biological Truth to the Federal Government Organizational Capacity and Record on Previous Grants – 20 points: The project proposal demonstrates that the organization has sufficient expertise, skills, and human resources to implement the project, including internal contr ols in place to manage federal funds. The organization demonstrates that it has a clear understanding of the underlying issue that the project will address. The organization demonstrates capacity for successful planning and responsible fiscal management. This includes a financial management system , a bank account , and if applicable, satisfactory audit findings. Applicants who have received grant funds previously have been compliant with applicable rules and regulations , including the Award Provisions and Standard Terms and Conditions. Where partners are described, the applicant details each partner’s respective role and provides curriculum vitae (CVs) for persons responsible for the project and financial administration. Proposed personnel, institutional resources, and partners are adequate and appropriate. Project Planning/Ability to Achieve Objectives – 25 points: The project plan is well developed, with sufficient detail about how activities will be carried out. The proposal specifies target audiences, participant recruitment, and geographic areas of implementation. The proposal outlines clear, achievable objectives. The proposal includes a reasonable implementation timeline. The project scope is appropriate and clearly defined. Budget – 15 points: The budget and narrative justification are sufficiently detailed. The budget demonstrates that the organization has devoted time to accurately determine expenses associated with the project instead of providing rough estimates. Costs are reasonable in relation to the proposed activities and anticipated results. The results and proposed outcomes justify the total cost of the project. Budget items are reasonable, allowable, and allocable. Monitoring and Evaluation – 10 points: There is a complete and thorough draft submission of a M&E Performance Monitoring Plan (PMP). This will include a list of proposed project activities, corresponding milestone, output, and outcome indicators, a description of data collection methods, and a timeline for collecting such information. The proposal presents a clear theory of change on how the program will address that problem. Funded projects will have their plans finalized during the negotiation phase, and monitoring plans may be subject to periodic updates throughout the life of the project. Sustainability – 10 points: The project proposal describes clearly the approach that will be used to ensure maximum sustainability or advancement of project goals after the end of project activity. 2. Indirect Costs If two or more applications receive equivalent scores based on the evaluation criteria outlined in this NOFO, preference will be given to the applicant with the lower indirect cost rate, as consistent with Executive Order 14332, Section 4(b)(iii). This preference will only be applied as a tie-breaking mechanism and does not supersede the primary evaluation criteria. 3. Review and Selection Process Acknowledgement of receipt. Applicants will receive acknowledgment of receipt of their proposal. Review. All submissions are screened for technical eligibility. If a submission is missing any required forms/documents listed above in Section D. Application Contents and Format , it will be considered ineligible and will not be reviewed by the grants review committee. A technical review panel will review eligible proposals based upon the criteria noted in this NOFO. Follow up notification. Applicants will generally be notified within 120 days after the NOFO deadline regarding the results of the review panel. 4.Risk Review i. Under the merit review as required by 2 CFR 200.206, prior to making a Federal Award the Department will review and consider the following risk factors: Financial stability Management systems and standards History of performance Audit reports and findings Ability to effectively implement project requirements ii. Responsibility/Qualification Information in SAM.gov Include the following language if the total Federal share of any award under this NOFO will be greater than the simplified acquisition threshold ($350,000): The Federal awarding agency, prior to making a Federal award with a total amount of Federal share greater than the simplified acquisition threshold, is required to review and consider any information about the applicant that is in the U.S. government designated integrity and performance system accessible through SAM.gov (see 41 U.S.C. 2313). An applicant can review and comment on any information in the responsibility/qualification records available in SAM.gov. Before making decisions in the risk review required by 2 CFR 200.206, the Department will consider any comments by the applicant, along with information available in the responsibility/qualification records in SAM.gov. iii. High Risk Designation Awardees that are deemed to be high risk based on the above risk factors will be held to special award conditions. At a minimum, the recipient and/or project designated as High Risk will be required to submit monthly narrative reports and/or quarterly detailed financial reports. Recipients may also be required, upon request of the Grants Officer or Grants Officer Representative, to provide electronic copies of receipts or other supporting documentation (e.g., timesheets, travel documents) for costs incurred. The Grants Officer may withhold 10% of the award amount until final reports have been reviewed and approved by the GO. The recipient may be required to pay all salaries supported by the grant via electronic funds transfer. Other special award conditions may also be included if deemed appropriate by the Grants Officer.   G. AWARD NOTICES The award or cooperative agreement will be written, signed, awarded, and administered by the Grants Officer. The award agreement is the authorizing document, and it will be provided to the recipient for review and counter-signature. The recipient may only start incurring project expenses beginning on the start date shown on the award document signed by the Grants Officer. If a proposal is selected for funding, the Department of State has no obligation to provide any additional future funding. Renewal of an award to increase funding or extend the period of performance is at the discretion of the Department of State. Issuance of this NOFO does not constitute an award commitment on the part of the U.S. government, nor does it commit the U.S. government to pay for costs incurred in the preparation and submission of proposals. Further, the U.S. government reserves the right to reject any or all proposals received. Payment Method: Recipients will be required to request payments by completing form SF-270—Request for Advance or Reimbursement and submitting the form to the Grants Officer and Grants Officer Representative. Recipients may not draw down funds without the affirmative authorization of the Department of State. In addition, recipients must submit, with each SF-270 payment request, a detailed explanation justifying the request. H. Post-Award Requirements and Administration 1. Administrative and National Policy Requirements Before submitting an application, applicants should review all the terms and conditions and required certifications which will apply to this award, to ensure that they will be able to comply. These include: In accordance with the Office of Management and Budget’s guidance located at 2 CFR part 200, all applicable Federal laws, and relevant Executive guidance, the Department of State will review and consider applications for funding, as applicable to specific programs, pursuant to this notice of funding opportunity in accordance with the following: Guidance for Grants and Agreements in Title 2 of the Code of Federal Regulations (2 CFR), as updated in the Federal Register’s 89 FR 30046 on April 22, 2024, particularly on: Selecting recipients most likely to be successful in delivering results based on the program objectives through an impartial process of evaluating Federal award applications (2 CFR part 200.205), Promoting the freedom of speech and religious liberty in alignment with Promoting Free Speech and Religious Liberty (E.O. 13798) and Improving Free Inquiry, Transparency, and Accountability at Colleges and Universities (E.O. 13864) (§§ 200.300, 200.303, 200.339, and 200.341), Providing a preference, to the extent permitted by law, to maximize use of goods, products, and materials produced in the United States (2 CFR part 200.322), and Terminating agreements pursuant to the U.S. Department of State Standard Terms and Conditions, including, to the greatest extent authorized by law, if an award no longer effectuates the program goals or agency priorities (2 CFR part 200.340). For the avoidance of doubt, the Department has sole discretion over the determination that an award no longer effectuates program goals or agency priorities, and this provision permits awards to be terminated at the Department’s convenience, including when it determines that the award no longer advances the national interest. 2 CFR 25 – UNIVERSAL IDENTIFIER AND SYSTEM FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT 2 CFR 170 – REPORTING SUBAWARD AND EXECUTIVE COMPENSATION INFORMATION 2 CFR 175 – AWARD TERM FOR TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS 2 CFR 182 – GOVERNMENTWIDE REQUIREMENTS FOR DRUG-FREE WORKPLACE (FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE) 2 CFR 183 – NEVER CONTRACT WITH THE ENEMY 2 CFR 600 – DEPARTMENT OF STATE REQUIREMENTS U.S. DEPARTMENT OF STATE STANDARD TERMS AND CONDITIONS Recipients must comply with all applicable Executive Orders. A searchable list can be found in the Federal Register: https://www.federalregister.gov/ . 2. Reporting Reporting Requirements: Recipients will be required to submit financial reports and program reports. The award document will specify what reports are required and how often these reports must be submitted. Note : most recipients will be required to submit quarterly program progress and financial reports throughout the project period. The quarterly progress report should include an up-to-date copy of the PMP datasheet. Progress and financial reports are due 30 days after the reporting period. Final certified programmatic and financial reports are due 120 days after the close of the project period. All reports are to be submitted electronically. The Awardee must also provide the AIT on an annual basis an inventory of all the U.S. government provided equipment using the SF428 form. Foreign Assistance Data Review: As required by Congress, the Department of State must make progress in its efforts to improve tracking and reporting of foreign assistance data through the Foreign Assistance Data Review (FADR). The FADR requires tracking of foreign assistance activity data from budgeting, planning, and allocation through obligation and disbursement. Successful applicants will be required to report and draw down federal funding based on the appropriate FADR Data Elements, indicated within their award documentation. In cases of more than one FADR Data Element, typically program or sector and/or regions or country, the successful applicant will be required to maintain separate accounting records. If the federal share of the award will include more than $500,000 over the period of performance, insert the following language: Applicants should be aware of the post award reporting requirements reflected in 2 CFR 200 Appendix XII—Award Term and Condition for Recipient Integrity and Performance Matters . 3.Branding and Marking The Department of State, its programs, and U.S. Government funding and assistance should be easily identifiable to the Department’s global audiences. Recipients of federal assistance awards must follow the branding guidance published at Guidance for Contracts and Grants – U.S. Department of State Brand System. Branding policy exceptions are outlined in the U.S. Department of State Foreign Affairs Manual 10 FAM 416, Policy Exceptions. For more information, visit: https://brand.america.gov/ I. Other Information Guidelines for Budget Justification Personnel and Fringe Benefits: Describe the wages, salaries, and benefits of temporary or permanent staff who will be working directly for the applicant on the program, and the percentage of their time that will be spent on the program. Travel: Estimate the costs of travel and per diem for this program, for program staff, consultants or speakers, and participants/beneficiaries. If the program involves international travel, include a brief statement of justification for that travel. Equipment: Describe any machinery, furniture, or other personal property that is required for the program, which has a useful life of more than one year (or a life longer than the duration of the program), and costs at least $10,000 per unit. Supplies: List and describe all the items and materials, including any computer devices, that are needed for the program. If an item costs more than $10,000 per unit, then put it in the budget under Equipment. Contractual: Describe goods and services that the applicant plans to acquire through a contract with a vendor. Also describe any sub-awards to non-profit partners that will help carry out the program activities. Other Direct Costs: Describe other costs directly associated with the program, which do not fit in the other categories. For example, shipping costs for materials and equipment or applicable taxes. All “Other” or “Miscellaneous” expenses must be itemized and explained. Indirect Costs: These are costs that cannot be linked directly to the program activities, such as overhead costs needed to help keep the organization operating. If your organization has a Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate (NICRA) and includes NICRA charges in the budget, attach a copy of your latest NICRA. Organizations that have never had a NICRA may request indirect costs of 15% of Modified Total Direct Costs (MTDC) as defined in 2 CFR 200.1. “Cost Sharing” refers to contributions from the organization or other entities other than AIT. It also includes in-kind contributions such as volunteers’ time and donated venues. Alcoholic Beverages: Please note that award funds cannot be used for alcoholic beverages and other entertainment related expenses. STEP Enrollment U.S. citizens who travel t o Taiwan are encouraged to enroll in the Department of State’s Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) available at: https://step.state.gov/step/ . Enrollment enables citizens to receive security-related messages from AIT and makes it easier for us to locate you in an emergency. AIT also recommends that all travelers review the State Department’s travel website at travel.state.gov for the Travel Warnings , Travel Alerts, and Taiwan Specific Information.   The post Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO): Implementation of 2027 GCTF Workshop in Eswatini appeared first on American Institute in Taiwan .

content:
2026 年 11 月 13 日

日本横须贺——

由军事海运司令部运营的远征快速运输舰俾斯麦市号（EPF 9）迎来了新任指挥官，中校。蒂亚·迈尔斯在横须贺舰队活动船上举行的仪式上。迈尔斯从中校手中接过指挥权。 VanAnh McCormick，在将该船移交给 MILCREW II 之前担任军事船员 I 的指挥官。

“从我们的人员流动开始，我们不再是 MILCREW II 和 CIVMAR；我们都是俾斯麦市号航空母舰，”迈尔斯在向由水手和公务员组成的混合船员发表的讲话中说道。 “‘保持媒体报道’是我们的全部工作！我们必须在场并准备好参与，同时互相支持，以确保我们的成功。Crew I 奠定了基础，我们的工作就是在此基础上继续发展。Possumus Efficiemus：我们可以而且我们将会实现。”

迈尔斯是南卡罗来纳州哥伦比亚人，2014 年从弗朗西斯马里恩大学毕业并获得数学学士学位后，被任命为海军军官。她还拥有海军研究生院的高级工商管理硕士学位。

在海上，迈尔斯曾在阿利伯克号航空母舰 (DDG 51)、珍珠港号航空母舰 (LSD 52) 和哈珀斯渡口号航空母舰 (LSD 49) 上服役。
在岸上，她在圣地亚哥海军水面和水雷作战发展中心和水面高级作战学校担任两栖作战战术教员。迈尔斯接替了麦考密克，麦考密克于 2026 年 7 月接管了 MILCREW I 的指挥权，并带领船员完成了有史以来的首次 EPF 部署。部署期间，船员航行超过4000海里，访问了4个海外港口。机组人员为“锐剑”演习提供了后勤保障，并完成了任务要求的所有准备工作。此外，供应部门还入围了 David M. Cook 食品服务卓越奖的决赛。

俾斯麦号是EPF级第九艘舰艇。这些浅吃水、全铝制商用双体船旨在以 35 节的平均速度将 600 短吨军用货物运输 1,200 海里。该船设有用于直升机操作的飞行甲板、车辆卸载坡道部署以及增强沿海操作和港口通道的浅吃水。这些能力使 EPF 能够在严峻或受损的港口提供灵活的物流支持、快速运输和救灾。

该船的船员由军事人员和文职海员组成。 MILCREW 轮流部署，基地设在圣地亚哥，而该舰的母港是横须贺，由美国第七舰队负责作战控制。
军事海运司令部负责指挥和支持大约 140 艘民用船只的行动，这些船只为美国海军舰船补充海上补给、执行专门任务、在全球范围内预置战斗货物、提供支持服务以及向部署的美国部队运输军事装备和补给品。

13 November 2026

YOKOSUKA, Japan --

The expeditionary fast transport USS City of Bismarck (EPF 9), operated by Military Sealift Command, welcomed its new commanding officer, Lt. Cmdr. Tia Myers, during a ceremony aboard the ship at Fleet Activities Yokosuka. Myers assumed command from Lt. Cmdr. VanAnh McCormick, who served as the Military Crew I commander before turning the ship over to MILCREW II.

“Starting with our turnover, we are no longer MILCREW II and CIVMARs; we are all USS City of Bismarck,” Myers said in her address to the hybrid crew of sailors and civil service mariners. “It is all of our job to ‘keep the press!’ We have to be present and ready to engage while supporting each other to ensure our success. Crew I laid the foundation, and it is our job to build upon it. Possumus Efficiemus: We can and we will accomplish.”

A native of Columbia, South Carolina, Myers commissioned as a naval officer in 2014 after graduating from Francis Marion University with a bachelor’s degree in mathematics. She also holds an executive master’s degree in business administration from the Naval Postgraduate School.

At sea, Myers served aboard USS Arleigh Burke (DDG 51), USS Pearl Harbor (LSD 52) and USS Harpers Ferry (LSD 49).

Ashore, she served as an amphibious warfare tactics instructor at the Naval Surface and Mine Warfighting Development Center and Surface Advanced Warfighting School in San Diego. Myers relieved McCormick, who took command of MILCREW I in July 2026 and led the crew through its first ever EPF deployment. During the deployment, the crew sailed more than 4,000 nautical miles and visited four overseas ports. The crew provided logistics support for Exercise Keen Sword and completed all ready for tasking requirements. In addition, the supply department became a finalist for the David M. Cook Food Service Excellence Award.

Bismarck is the ninth ship in the EPF class. These shallow-draft, all-aluminum, commercial-based catamarans are designed to transport 600 short tons of military cargo 1,200 nautical miles at an average speed of 35 knots. The ship features a flight deck for helicopter operations, a vehicle offload ramp deployment, and a shallow draft that enhances littoral operations and port access. These capabilities allow the EPF to deliver flexible logistics support, rapid transport and disaster relief in austere or damaged ports.

The ship operates with a hybrid crew of military personnel and civil service mariners. The MILCREWs rotate for deployments and are based in San Diego, while the ship is homeported in Yokosuka under the operational control of U.S. 7th Fleet.

Military Sealift Command directs and supports operations for approximately 140 civilian-crewed ships that replenish U.S. Navy ships at sea, conduct specialized missions, preposition combat cargo worldwide, provide support services, and transport military equipment and supplies to deployed U.S. forces.

SilentAir 劫持亚洲电信网络拦截 SMS 2FA 代码并监视台湾用户
SilentAir 劫持亚洲电信网络拦截 SMS 2FA 代码并监视台湾用户
Swati Khandelwal报告2026年11月13日网络间谍/威胁情报
一个新发现的间谍组织利用亚洲移动运营商内部的黑客设备拦截特定人员的电话和短信，这些人员大多来自台湾。
总部位于斯德哥尔摩的电信和网络安全软件公司 Enea 本周在至少六个亚洲国家发现了该组织的攻击源，并将其命名为 SilentAir。它高度确信 SilentAir 是一个国家级行为者，但仅将其活动与中国联系起来，信心度较低。
该公司已告知运营商其在何处找到 SilentAir 源。据称，SilentAir 目前已中断，但可能会恢复。报告没有透露这些运营商是否已经清理了被黑的设备。
移动运营商使用 SS7 和 Diameter 协议来交换路由呼叫和文本并启用漫游的信令消息。此流量穿过称为 IPX 的共享网络，该网络在运营商之间的高度信任基础上运行。 SilentAir 从被黑设备向 IPX 发送攻击。
为了进行拦截，SilentAir 向目标的家庭网络发送了 UpdateLocation 消息或其等效的 Diameter 消息。该消息声称，被黑客入侵的设备现在正在为目标的手机提供服务。如果家庭网络接受它，该人的电话和短信将被转移给攻击者。
其中一些攻击有效。对于某些目标，该公司观察到两因素身份验证（2FA）代码在转移生效后立即被拦截。这表明有人试图闯入这些人注册的其他帐户。
该报告没有提供类似的语音通话证据，也没有说明是否有任何帐户被盗用。
该公司从 SilentAir 看到的攻击中，拦截占 18.3%。对于典型的监控公司（大多数信号攻击背后的公司）来说，该公司早期研究中的份额为 2.1%。
一些目标是本国的政治和政府要人。在极少数情况下，多个国家的 SilentAir 设备会协同对抗此类目标，该公司表示，这些目标指向单个控制器。
攻击呈爆发式发生，一个月内从一个或几个订户到数千个订户，两次爆发之间的间隔长达几个月或更长时间。
在台湾以外，目标主要位于其他东南亚和东亚网络，有时也位于东非、中亚、中东和欧洲。使用被黑客攻击的运营商自己的网络的人也可能成为目标，但该公司无法看到该流量。
该公司通过研究针对运营商之间链路的攻击发现了 SilentAir。自 2025 年初以来，它一直在追踪来自一些通常不会发送攻击的亚洲运营商的异常攻击，其中大部分是通过 SS7，有时是通过 Diameter。后来的分析甚至更早地发现了可疑活动。
根据该公司的技术报告，托管 SilentAir 的网络以奇怪且不一致的方式处理转移目标的后续消息。这就留下了两种解释：外部有人伪造了这些网络的信令地址，或者每个网络内部的设备已被接管。

【原文 English Original】
SilentAir Hijacks Asian Telecom Networks to Intercept SMS 2FA Codes and Spy on Taiwanese Users
SilentAir Hijacks Asian Telecom Networks to Intercept SMS 2FA Codes and Spy on Taiwanese Users
Swati KhandelwalNov 13, 2026Cyber Espionage / Threat Intelligence
A newly identified spying group used hacked equipment inside Asian mobile operators to intercept the calls and texts of selected people, mostly in Taiwan.
Enea, a telecom and cybersecurity software company based in Stockholm, found the group's attack sources in at least six Asian countries and named it SilentAir this week. It assessed with high confidence that SilentAir is a state-level actor, but linked its activity to China only with low confidence.
The company has told the operators where it found SilentAir sources. It said SilentAir has been disrupted for now but could return. The report does not say whether those operators have cleaned up the hacked equipment.
Mobile operators use the SS7 and Diameter protocols to exchange signaling messages that route calls and texts and enable roaming. This traffic crosses a shared network called the IPX, which runs on a high level of trust between operators. SilentAir sent its attacks into the IPX from the hacked equipment.
For interception, SilentAir sent the target's home network an UpdateLocation message, or its Diameter equivalent. The message claimed that the hacked equipment was now serving the target's phone. If the home network accepted it, calls and texts for that person would be diverted to the attackers.
Some of these attacks worked. For some targets, the company observed two-factor authentication (2FA) codes being intercepted immediately after the diversion took effect. That points to an attempt to break into other accounts registered to those people.
The report gives no similar evidence for voice calls, and it does not say whether any account was taken over.
Interception made up 18.3% of the attacks the company saw from SilentAir. For a typical surveillance company, the kind of firm behind most signaling attacks, the share was 2.1% in the company's earlier research.
Some targets were political and government VIPs in their own countries. In rare cases, SilentAir equipment in several countries worked together against such targets, which the company said points to a single controller.
The attacks came in bursts, from one or a few subscribers to several thousand over a month, with gaps of up to several months or longer between bursts.
Outside Taiwan, targets were mostly in other Southeast and East Asian networks, and at times in East Africa, Central Asia, the Middle East, and Europe. People using the hacked operators' own networks may also have been targeted, but the company could not see that traffic.
The company spotted SilentAir by studying attacks on the links between operators. Since early 2025, it has tracked unusual attacks, mostly over SS7 and sometimes Diameter, from some Asian operators that would not normally send attacks. Later analysis found suspicious activity even earlier.
The networks hosting SilentAir handled follow-up messages for diverted targets in odd and inconsistent ways, according to the company's technical report. That left two explanations: someone outside was faking those networks' signaling addresses, or equipment inside each network had been taken over.
The company then saw equipment inside one operator both send and receive attack commands, which confirmed the second explanation. That equipment behaved exactly like SilentAir sources in other networks.
Detecting and blocking the attacks was hard at first because the attackers understood mobile networks and signaling defenses well. After the attacks were contained, the company recovered traces of unauthorized access. It could not analyze the malware it believes SilentAir used.
The report does not name the countries, the operators, or any of the targets. In some countries, SilentAir attacks came from more than one operator.
SilentAir also sent silent SMS on a very large scale, mainly to subscribers in Taiwan. These are texts that the phone does not display or alert on.
During the day, most silent SMS went to subscribers on other networks, such as Southeast Asian networks. One of their main uses appears to have been checking whether a diversion had worked, the company said.
If the test text reached the hacked equipment instead of the phone, the attackers knew they were getting that person's texts.
Most silent SMS went out at night, and most of those went to people in Taiwan. The company said the purpose of those messages is not confirmed. They may be a bulk check that earlier diversions were still in place, since phones are least likely to re-register to their real location at night.
The silent texts carried spam-like motivational or promotional lines, often in English. The company believes the text was a disguise. If an operator along the way stripped a message's silent setting, the recipient would see it as spam and ignore it.
The company's low-confidence link to China rests on several signs. SilentAir focused on Taiwan and did not target Chinese networks or subscribers.
Its tracking and interception attacks also followed a working day in UTC+8, which is China Standard Time. They started at 9 a.m., almost stopped on weekends, and paused or slowed around Chinese holidays.
The company also considered a link to Liminal Panda, a group behind earlier telecom intrusions. It called the link possible but unconfirmed and does not tie the two groups together for now.
In several hacked operators, SilentAir attacks happened during a known Liminal Panda infection. At other times, the two showed no sign of working together. They also went after operators in the same part of Asia, though Liminal Panda has no known focus on Taiwan.
SilentAir's behavior also partly matches that of SCTPE, a little-known Linux trojan that runs in the kernel and is designed to send and receive SS7 and Diameter traffic.
Singapore's Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) has described the same tool in a government advisory. There, the tool is called SIGweaver. The agency said CrowdStrike identified it on January 21 and links it to Liminal Panda with moderate confidence.
But Enea said SilentAir answered messages it had not sent itself, which the known SCTPE program cannot do. SilentAir's operational security also seemed far better than Liminal Panda's.
Separately, the company's GTP firewall has detected Liminal Panda activity at several customer operators since the first quarter of this year. The company blocked the group's GTPDoor traffic there and saw Liminal Panda infections, or strong signs of them, in at least 5 to 10 operators.
The GTPDoor backdoor, first documented on February 27, 2024, hides commands within GTP-C, the protocol that establishes mobile data connections between networks. The company also found evidence of a new version that hides commands in GTP-U, the part of GTP that carries users' data. GTP-U traffic is harder to inspect, though the company believes the new version serves mainly as a backup.
The company said any attacker could reuse these techniques, and it told operators to:
Deploy GTP-C and GTP-U firewalls and configure them to share information with their SS7 and Diameter firewalls.
Go beyond the industry's basic recommendations for signaling security.
Treat the whole IPX as untrusted.
Add detection for signaling protocols inside their own networks.
Connect signaling security with the rest of their IT security.
The report does not advise people whose calls and texts may be targeted.

全球 Microsoft 365 中断导致 74 个国家/地区的服务中断 |中国劳工公告栏
星期六, 14 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
全球 Microsoft 365 中断导致 74 个国家/地区的服务中断
11 月 13 日，微软的云生产力套件遭遇大规模全球系统中断，导致至少 74 个国家和地区的电子邮件、消息传递和人工智能服务瘫痪。香港航空公司表示，航班时刻表保持正常，但警告可能出现通讯延误。
据 The Standard 报道，11 月 13 日上午，微软的云生产力套件发生了大规模的全球系统中断，导致至少 74 个国家和地区的电子邮件、消息传递和人工智能服务瘫痪。
尽管 Microsoft 365 云服务在全球范围内出现广泛中断，香港主要客运航空公司确认其航班时刻表于 11 月 13 日保持正常，但航空公司警告旅客可能出现通信延误和后台中断。
这次中断影响了全球用户，电子邮件、消息平台和人工智能工具等服务都无法访问。此次中断的规模至少覆盖 74 个国家，凸显了全球企业和政府运营对微软云基础设施的依赖。
在另一项进展中，英伟达表示，美国的出口管制实际上将其排除在中国人工智能数据中心市场之外，但路透社的一份评论发现，围绕这家美国芯片制造商的受限处理器构建的中国计算项目价值超过 30 亿美元。
特朗普政府发言人表示，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普的人工智能特别工作组成员于周四举行会议，讨论了鼓励美国关键部门报告人工智能网络攻击的方法。
在周五举行的2026星岛全球经济峰会上，香港科技大学计算机科学与工程系讲座教授贾家亚认为，人工智能的发展虽然深刻改变了工作模式，但不会造成大规模失业，而是会创造大量新的就业机会。

Saturday, 14 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Global Microsoft 365 outage disrupts services across 74 countries
A massive global system outage struck Microsoft's cloud productivity suite on 13 November, crippling email, messaging and AI services across at least 74 countries and territories. Hong Kong airlines said flight schedules remained normal but warned of possible communication delays.
A massive global system outage struck Microsoft's cloud productivity suite on the morning of 13 November, crippling email, messaging, and artificial intelligence services across at least 74 countries and territories, according to The Standard.
Hong Kong's major passenger airlines confirmed that their flight schedules remained normal on 13 November following the widespread global disruption across Microsoft 365 cloud services, though carriers warned travellers of possible communication delays and back-office disruptions.
The outage affected users worldwide, with services including email, messaging platforms and AI tools rendered inaccessible. The scale of the disruption, covering at least 74 nations, highlighted the reliance on Microsoft's cloud infrastructure for business and government operations globally.
In a separate development, Nvidia has said US export controls have effectively shut it out of China's AI data-centre market, but a Reuters review has identified more than US$3 billion in Chinese computing projects built around the American chipmaker's restricted processors.
Members of US President Donald Trump's AI task force met on Thursday and discussed ways to encourage critical US sectors to report AI-powered cyberattacks, according to a Trump administration spokesperson.
At the Sing Tao Global Economic Summit 2026 on Friday, Jia Jiaya, Chair Professor of Department of Computer Science and Engineering at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, maintained that the development of artificial intelligence will not cause large-scale unemployment despite profoundly shifting work patterns, but rather create numerous new jobs.

星期六, 14 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
金管局表示，在微软宕机的情况下，香港银行仍保持正常运营
香港银行业监管机构表示，在全球微软服务中断后，所有零售银行的关键系统均运行正常。当局警告公众警惕利用该事件的诈骗者，银行业协会建议不要点击可疑链接或共享个人信息
2026 年 11 月 13 日 19:52 香港时间 · 更新于 11 月 14 日 04:24 · 阅读时间 1 分钟
香港金融管理局 (HKMA) 于 11 月 13 日表示，其意识到全球服务中断影响了部分微软服务，并正在密切关注事态及其对银行服务的潜在影响。管理局发言人表示，香港零售银行的所有关键系统，包括存款和转账功能均维持正常运作。金管局表示将继续与银行保持密切沟通并监察事态发展。
金管局提醒市民提高警惕，谨防骗徒利用事件冒充提供技术支持，以获取账户登入资料。它还警告人们不要点击可疑的超链接或向任何人透露支付卡数据、登录密码或一次性密码等敏感信息。
香港银行公会还呼吁公众提高警惕，警惕不法分子利用该事件发送欺诈信息的可能性。该协会表示，诈骗者可能冒充微软、银行或相关机构，利用系统故障或更新作为借口，发送要求立即采取行动的网络钓鱼消息，试图获取个人或财务信息。
该协会呼吁公众在收到据称来自银行的信息时仔细核实发件人的身份，不要点击可疑链接或打开可疑附件。它还建议不要通过未经验证的渠道登录帐户或提供个人信息。任何收到自称来自银行的可疑消息的人应直接联系相关银行以确认其真实性。

Hong Kong banks maintain normal operations amid Microsoft outage, HKMA says
Hong Kong's banking regulator says all retail banks' critical systems are functioning normally after a global Microsoft services outage. The authority warns the public to watch for scammers exploiting the incident, and the Banking Association advises against clicking suspicious links or sharing pers
13 Nov 2026 at 19:52 HKT · updated 14 Nov, 04:24 · 1 min read
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) said on 13 November that it is aware of a global disruption affecting some Microsoft services and is closely monitoring the situation and its potential impact on banking services. A spokesperson for the authority stated that all critical systems of retail banks in Hong Kong, including deposit and transfer functions, are maintaining normal operations. The HKMA said it will continue to maintain close communication with banks and monitor developments.
The HKMA reminded the public to stay vigilant against scammers who may use the incident to pretend to offer technical support in an attempt to obtain account login details. It also warned people not to click on suspicious hyperlinks or disclose sensitive information such as payment card data, login passwords or one-time passwords to anyone.
The Hong Kong Banking Association also urged the public to be alert to the possibility of criminals sending fraudulent messages exploiting the incident. The association said scammers may impersonate Microsoft, banks or related institutions, using system faults or updates as a pretext to send phishing messages that demand immediate action, in an attempt to obtain personal or financial information.
The association called on the public to carefully verify the identity of senders when receiving messages purportedly from banks, and not to click on suspicious links or open questionable attachments. It also advised against logging into accounts or providing personal information through unverified channels. Anyone receiving a suspicious message claiming to be from a bank should contact the relevant bank directly to confirm its authenticity.

香港卫生防护中心（CHP）11月13日表示，正在调查一起涉及一名34岁男子的输入性猴痘病例。患者上周出现发烧、疲劳和手臂皮疹，随后皮疹扩散到身体的其他部位。周三，他到伊丽莎白女王医院急症室寻求治疗，并入院接受隔离治疗。目前他的病情稳定。

Hong Kong reports imported monkeypox case, man had high-risk contact abroad
Hong Kong's Centre for Health Protection is investigating an imported monkeypox case involving a 34-year-old man who developed symptoms last week and is now in stable condition in hospital. The patient reported high-risk sexual contact with other men during the incubation period while outside Hong K
13 Nov 2026 at 19:30 HKT · updated 14 Nov, 04:24 · 1 min read
Hong Kong's Centre for Health Protection (CHP) said on 13 November it is investigating an imported case of monkeypox involving a 34-year-old man. The patient developed a fever, fatigue and a rash on his arm last week, with the rash later spreading to other parts of his body. He sought treatment at Queen Elizabeth Hospital's accident and emergency department on Wednesday and was admitted for isolation treatment. His condition is now stable.
The CHP said clinical samples tested by its Public Health Laboratory Services branch confirmed the patient was positive for the monkeypox virus. According to information provided by the patient, he had high-risk sexual contact with other men during the incubation period while outside Hong Kong. The CHP is continuing its epidemiological investigation into the case and will report it to the World Health Organization.
The CHP advised members of high-risk target groups to receive the monkeypox vaccine. It also urged the public to remain vigilant and avoid close physical contact with people suspected of being infected with monkeypox.
